# MAP / Page Identity & Navigation — Workflows and Feature Hierarchies
Corpus: `/mnt/c/Users/manci/PROJECTS/concur-corpus/CONCUR_INVOICE`, SAP 2026_08, Professional Edition, crawled 2026-08-29.
Both guide dirs swept with equal weight: admin-guides (1209 files), tools-guides (650 files).
Release notes read only for corroboration; **never cited as a sourceFile**.
Every quote below was verified by exact substring count against its file before emission.

## VERDICT IN ONE LINE

Two pages, both real, both siblings under `Administration > Invoice`, and both confirmed
against the corpus rather than taken on trust from the recon:
**Workflows** — ONE page, SEVEN tabs, `documentedBasis: rich`, `coverage: good`.
**Feature Hierarchies** — its own page, NOT a Workflows tab and NOT a Routing Configuration tab,
`documentedBasis: sparse`, `coverage: partial`, and thin **for a documented reason**.

---

## 1. WORKFLOWS

### 1.1 Page-hood — CONFIRMED, not re-opened

I reproduced the recon's three mechanical claims independently and all three hold.

**(i) Left-menu census, both dirs.** A broad census (`[A-Z][A-Za-z0-9 &/,'-]{2,55}\(left menu\)`,
prefix-stripped) returns **23 distinct labels**:

```
10 Forms and Fields      4 Invoice Settings      2 Tax Administration        1 Site Settings
 8 Workflows             4 Group Configurations  2 Purchase Order Matching   1 Polices  [sic]
 7 Attendees             4 Audit Rules           2 Policies                  1 Localization
                         3 List Management       2 Image Handling            1 Invoice Preferences
 1 Vendor Search Admin   1 User Permissions      1 User Administration       1 Feature Hierarchies
 1 Expense Type Import   1 Delegate Configurations                           1 Company Locations
 1 Company Admin, and then click User Permissions
```

`Workflows` scores 8. **Every candidate tab scores ZERO as a left-menu label** — verified
individually: `Approval Statuses (left menu)` 0, `Authorized Approvers (left menu)` 0,
`Email Notifications (left menu)` 0, `Confirmation Agreements (left menu)` 0,
`Reason Category and Codes (left menu)` 0. And **`Steps tab` = 0 corpus-wide**, as does
`Step Rules tab` and `General tab`, while `Steps page` = 10 files, `Step Rules page` = 5,
`General page` = 8 — the wizard is pages-inside-a-modal, never tabs.

> My census returns 23 labels, not the 30 the brief quotes. The difference is a regex-shape
> difference (mine strips the leading verb and folds `Administration > Invoice > X (left menu)`
> into `X`), not a disagreement about the workflow domain. **The load-bearing counts —
> Workflows 8, Feature Hierarchies 1, every tab 0 — are identical.** Recording the discrepancy
> rather than papering over it.

**(ii) One role gate for the whole surface.** `"This portion of the configuration requires
permissions for the Workflows section in Administration."` appears verbatim in exactly two files
(`step-2-activate-the-feature-27a421e2.md`, `step-3-edit-the-workflow-steps-f2731590.md`) — the
*section*, never a tab. The tool-level gate is `workflows-tool-8b3b4dbe.md`: Global and Group
Invoice Configuration administrator.

**(iii) The definitive sentence.** `access-workflow-fa9892a7.md`:
`"The Workflows tab on the Workflows page appears."` A tab named for its page — the Audit Rules
shape exactly. Reinforced by a **third independent page enumeration** in
`administrator-experience-8b302852.md`: *"The Configuration administrator will see the following
pages in Invoice Administrator related to image handling configuration:"* → Image Handling,
Policies, **Workflows**. All three are pages in this graph or (Workflows) becoming one.

**No page node is created for any tab, sub-tab, wizard page (General / Steps / Step Rules), or
dialog.** The four `workflow-guides-*.md` files are index tables of *external* setup guides and
get no node.

### 1.4 THE NBSP HAZARD — how I handled it, and why the emitted quotes look truncated

Roughly 40% of nav sentences in this corpus have **no `>` glyph at all**; the separators are two
consecutive U+00A0. Confirmed here by reading the bytes:

```
allowing-automatic-transmittal-of-purchase-orders-0f2e7fae.md
  'Administration\xa0\xa0Invoice\xa0\xa0Workflows\xa0\xa0Workflows tab'
preventing-po-transmittal-...-51b11602.md
  'Administration\xa0\xa0Invoice\xa0\xa0Workflows\xa0\xa0Settings tab'
hierarchies-7f68a876.md
  'Administration\xa0\xa0Invoice\xa0\xa0Hierarchies (explained below).'
professional-edition-fb3e6aa2.md
  'Administration \xa0\xa0Invoice \xa0\xa0Feature Hierarchies.'   <-- note the extra ASCII space
overview-9c8ca06e.md
  'accesses Workflows\xa0\xa0Reason Category and Codes'
access-workflow-fa9892a7.md
  'ClickAdministration\xa0\xa0Invoice.'                          <-- and no space after "Click"
```

I verified every one of these NBSP forms with an exact byte-level substring count and they all
return 1. **But I deliberately emitted the NBSP-free contiguous fragment on the far side of the
separator** (e.g. `"Settings tab and is shown in the following figure."`, `"Workflows tab by
opening a PR workflow and selecting the Allow employee to automatically transmit Purchase
Orders option."`, `"Feature Hierarchies before selection via the Policy tool."`) rather than a
quote that crosses the arrow. Reason: NBSP survives a byte-exact grep but is exactly the
character most likely to be normalised in transit between this agent and the validator, and
`NO QUOTE, NO NODE` is a harder failure than a slightly shorter quote. The full NBSP forms are
recorded here in the survey so nothing is lost.

Two extra text traps found in this group:
* `ClickAdministration` with **no space** in `access-workflow-fa9892a7.md` (once).
* `Worflows` misspelled once corpus-wide, in the very revision-history line that decides
  uiVariant (`general-information-8b3b0308.md`, September 19 2025).

### 1.7 uiVariant — `undifferentiated`, and that is the honest answer

There is **no `*-new-experience-*` twin for any workflow file**; `ls | grep -i new-experience`
returns 5 files corpus-wide, none in this domain. Two dated statements point in opposite
directions inside one corpus version:

* `general-information-8b3b0308.md`, **September 19 2025**: *"Updated images and text to the new
  UI for the Workflows Tool and Edit and Delete Worflows, Properties, and Steps sections."*
  → the missing twin is a **replacement**, revised in place, not a coverage gap.
* `tools-guides/how-single-step-approval-workflow-works-40145f24.md`: *"the Invoice Configuration
  administrator uses the Authorized Approvers link from workflows in the classic interface"*
  → the documented route is the **classic** interface.

**The corpus cannot settle which UI generation the click paths describe.** This matters more than
any field: navigation is the only knowledge this build produces that a Chromium driver cannot
re-derive, so if the paths describe a superseded UI, every navPath is wrong at once.
`uiVariant: "undifferentiated"`. **Not "both"** — three unearned "both" claims are already
outstanding debt in this graph (`page.audit-rules` still carries one).

## 2. FEATURE HIERARCHIES

### 2.1 Page-hood — CONFIRMED. It belongs to NEITHER Workflows NOR Routing Configuration.

* **Own left-menu entry**, one of only two unbuilt labels in the census:
  `tools-guides/step-2-associate-the-feature-hierarchy-to-the-source-list-bcaf1f5a.md` —
  *"Click Feature Hierarchies (left menu)."*
* **Own role gate, worded exactly like the Workflows gate and stated in contrast to it inside a
  single numbered flow.** `step-1-define-the-cost-object-approver-hierarchy-6e7b7dc6.md`:
  *"This portion of the configuration requires permissions for the Feature Hierarchies section in
  Administration."* — while step 2 of that same flow
  (`step-2-activate-the-feature-27a421e2.md`) says *"…permissions for the **Workflows** section in
  Administration."* **Two gates, two peer surfaces, in SAP's own contrast.** Corpus-wide, the
  string `"permissions for the Feature Hierarchies section in Administration"` returns exactly 1
  file and `"permissions for the Workflows section in Administration"` exactly 2 — and they are
  steps 1 and 2/3 of one procedure.
* **Peer-tool evidence (identity, not navigation).** `tools-guides/overview-of-steps-37e3c289.md`:
  *"The administrator uses the following tools in the order presented to configure the feature."*
  then Step 1 List Management, **Step 2 Feature Hierarchies**, Step 3 Group Configurations,
  Step 4 Forms and Fields, Step 5 Vendor Employee Access Import, Step 6 User Administration.
  Three of those are already pages in this graph. That is first-class page-hood evidence, and
  per the critic it belongs in identityNotes, **not** navPathEvidence — "Step 2: Feature
  Hierarchies" is a list item, not a click.
* **It is never a tab of anything.** No file writes "Feature Hierarchies tab".

### 2.2 Navigation — no middle segment, and the node is UNATTESTED (not absent)

Both documented paths run `Administration > Invoice > Feature Hierarchies`:

1. `tools-guides/step-2-associate-…-bcaf1f5a.md` — *"Click Administration  Invoice."* →
   *"Click Feature Hierarchies (left menu)."* → *"On the Feature Hierarchies, select _Invoice
   Vendor Employee Access_, and then click Modify Hierarchy."*
2. `professional-edition-fb3e6aa2.md` — *"Go to Administration  Invoice  Feature
   Hierarchies."* → *"Select the Invoice Payment feature name."* → *"Select Modify Hierarchy."*

I ran `grep -rn "Invoice Processing Admin"` over both dirs: **31 hits, not one of them Feature
Hierarchies.** The middle node is therefore **UNATTESTED for this page — record as unattested,
not absent.** The left-menu entry is a **SIBLING of Workflows, not a child.**
**A driver told to reach Feature Hierarchies via a Workflows path WILL FAIL.** That is an active
harm, not a filing preference.

**Menu-label alias no prior artefact records:** `hierarchies-7f68a876.md` writes the label as
plain **"Hierarchies"** — *"…first configure their hierarchy structure in
Administration  Invoice  Hierarchies (explained below)."* Per the critic, the
verifying fragment `"Hierarchies (explained below)."` does **not** carry the path (the path is in
the preceding NBSP-separated clause), so it is emitted as an **aliases citation**, not as
navPathEvidence. Third alias form: `overview-8b2edfd0.md` writes *"the Feature Hierarchies section
of Administration"* and `create-the-invoice-routing-feature-hierarchy-8b510285.md` writes *"the
Feature Hierarchies area"*.

### 2.3 Why it is SHARED — build once, point at it twice

One page hosts at least five named feature hierarchies serving four config domains:

| Feature hierarchy | Consumer | Evidence |
|---|---|---|
| Invoice Routing | **Routing Configuration** (BUILT, G2) | `create-the-invoice-routing-feature-hierarchy-8b510285.md` |
| Invoice Payment | payment groups | `professional-edition-fb3e6aa2.md` "Select the Invoice Payment feature name." |
| Invoice Vendor Employee Access | vendor groups / Group Configurations (BUILT, G1) | `step-2-associate-…-bcaf1f5a.md` |
| Payment Authorized Approver | **Workflows > Authorized Approvers** | `understand-the-hierarchy-b65d7089.md`, `user-administrator-fcfd570c.md` "Authorized Approver Feature Hierarchy" |
| Cost Object Approver | **Workflows** General page | `step-1-define-the-cost-object-approver-hierarchy-6e7b7dc6.md` |

Folding it into Workflows would mis-file routing and vendor access; folding it into Routing
Configuration would mis-file the COA hierarchy only Workflows uses.

**HARD FORWARD REFERENCE INTO THE WORKFLOWS BUILD** — `understand-the-hierarchy-b65d7089.md`:
*"You must define the authorized approver hierarchy (Invoice > Feature Hierarchies)"* and
import/create its source list **before the authorized approver feature can be activated**. Emit
that edge: Workflows > Authorized Approvers > Configuration tab
(`Authorized Approver feature is available for workflows`) is **blocked** on this page.
Second forward reference, `workflow-667cee21.md`: PR hierarchies *"must be configured using
Invoice  Feature Hierarchies before selection via the Policy tool."*

### 2.4 The four endpoints it resolves — all of them the SAME field

*"In the Source List, select the name of the list you created in Step 1"*

### 2.5 documentedBasis: **sparse** / coverage: **partial** — and WHY

12-file core, 23,239 B. Expect roughly **five fields**: Source List, Level, Segment Name, the
feature-name selector, Modify Hierarchy. That is the whole documented control surface.

**SAP files the substance in the external _Shared: Feature Hierarchies Setup Guide_, which is NOT
in this corpus.** That guide is referenced by name in at least eight files
(`create-hierarchy-and-import-connected-list-data-c6ab8a52.md`, `details-section-49500221.md`,

`workflow-creation-process-1d37b85f.md`). **Thin with a documented reason is a correct, publishable
answer.** This page is being told so before the field extraction starts specifically so it does
not manufacture fields around the gap — the Budget Configuration failure mode.

fields.name: source_list
fields.label: Source List
fields.sourceQuote: In the Source List, select the name of the list you created in Step 1
fields.notes: THE ONE FIELD THIS PAGE DOCUMENTS WELL, and the single field that resolves all four already-written forward endpoints into this page (dep.g1.061, dep.g2.003, dep.g5g5.050, dep.g5g5.051). Exact field name per the corpus is 'Source List'. validValues is EMPTY BY CONSTRUCTION AND CORRECTLY SO: the options are the tenant's own List Management lists, so no documented list can enumerate them and inventing any would be a tenant-specific value - forbidden by the blind-build rule. What IS documented is the option's PROVENANCE and a hard cardinality rule. Provenance: the list must already exist in List Management before it can be selected here ('Create the source list, match to Vendor Employee Access.', tools-guides/step-1-create-the-source-list-in-list-management-cc91aa73.md); admin-guides/professional-edition-fb3e6aa2.md states the same as a precondition for the Invoice Payment hierarchy - 'The source list and custom field referenced in the steps below must already be configured before you proceed.' Cardinality rule: 'If a multi-level list was created, be sure to add additional levels and segments to match the list levels.' (bcaf1f5a) - the shape of the chosen list DICTATES how many Level/Segment Name rows must be created here. Wording drifts by feature: bcaf1f5a says 'In the Source List, select the name of the list you created in Step 1'; fb3e6aa2 says 'Select the source list to use to identify the various funding accounts.'; 8b510285 says 'A source list is required to map the hierarchy path segments for use.' Same control, three feature contexts. [MERGE] Cross-lens duplicate 'sourceList' (tables lens) carried the identical sourceFile and identical verbatim sourceQuote and was folded into this single record under the canonical snake_case name; no second node emitted. Both refuters returned disposition keep with verbatimVariantIndex 0, and I re-confirmed grep -F -c = 1 for the sourceQuote and for every quote embedded in these notes. Label MUST stay exactly 'Source List' so the four already-written endpoints dep.g1.061, dep.g2.003, dep.g5g5.050 and dep.g5g5.051 resolve here.

fields.name: level
fields.label: Level
fields.sourceQuote: Click New to add Employee as the value for Level (this is the default and cannot be changed).
fields.notes: THE CORPUS CONTRADICTS ITSELF ON THIS CONTROL AND I HAVE NOT RECONCILED IT - see contradictions[0]. For the Invoice Vendor Employee Access feature hierarchy the value is 'Employee' and bcaf1f5a says explicitly it 'is the default and cannot be changed'; for the Invoice Payment feature hierarchy professional-edition-fb3e6aa2.md says 'Set the level to Request.', which is an ACT OF SETTING, i.e. changeable. Both readings are recorded as separate context-scoped value sets keyed on feature_name. Most likely provisioning/feature-dependent: what the level control offers varies with which feature hierarchy is selected. validValues left EMPTY at field level on purpose so neither reading is silently promoted to the whole page. fieldType 'unknown' because no file states the widget - it may be a fixed display for Employee and a selector for Request. SEPARATELY, 'Level' has a documented DEPTH range of 1..10 for the Invoice Vendor Employee Access source list, attested identically in two import specs ('Level 1 of the source list attached to the Invoice Vendor Employee Access feature hierarchy.' through Level 10, the-import-template-fields-and-descriptions-8b51ca3d.md and vendor-group-mapping-record-type-310-6eb8ffdc.md) - that is IMPORT-RECORD depth, not a value list for this page control, and per instruction I did NOT re-emit the Group 5 Level value set. [REPAIR APPLIED] Defect named by refuter 1 of 2: the procedure-lens and tables-lens variants both set fieldType 'dropdown', which this record's OWN sourceQuote contradicts - 'Click New to add Employee as the value for Level (this is the default and cannot be changed).' A control the cited file says cannot be changed is not attested as a selectable dropdown. fieldType is therefore 'unknown' (the crosscut lens's own honest value and a legal type here): no corpus file states the widget, and the two documented contexts behave differently - fixed 'Employee' for Invoice Vendor Employee Access (bcaf1f5a) versus an act of setting, 'Set the level to Request.' (admin-guides/professional-edition-fb3e6aa2.md, grep -F -c = 1). validValues stays [] and BOTH context-scoped readings plus the contradiction node are kept unreconciled, per the governing constraint. Unresolved internal tension retained: step 5 of bcaf1f5a says the value cannot be changed while step 7 of the same file says 'If you intend to use multi-level named vendor groups (Level 1; Level 2; Level 3) add additional levels and segments now to match.' - so more than one Level row is evidently creatable. [HOMONYM GUARD, refuter 2] The built page.accounting-administration owns segment_level (label 'Level', validValues Request / Line Item / Allocation, from adding-a-new-segment-d6dfb07b.md). Its 'Request' and this page's 'Set the level to Request.' are an ACUTE near-miss: a merge keyed on label+value would fuse two unrelated hierarchy editors. Keeping validValues empty here is what prevents that. grep -F -c for 'Line Item', 'Allocation', 'Country', 'Org Unit', 'Policy Name' and 'Custom 1' all return 0 in BOTH Feature Hierarchies files - none of that value set is attested here.

fields.name: segment_name
fields.label: Segment Name
fields.sourceQuote: In the Segment Name list, select the field that will act as the list in User Permissions
fields.notes: The field chosen as each hierarchy path segment, paired one-to-one with a Level row. validValues EMPTY: the options are the site's own form fields (Custom NN), so no documented list can enumerate them without becoming tenant-specific. Documented behaviour instead: (a) it selects the field that surfaces the choice downstream - 'In the Segment Name list, select the field that will act as the list in User Permissions from which you will select the vendor access group for your user.' (bcaf1f5a); (b) the example uses a renamed Custom field, and the rename is a LATER, OPTIONAL step on a DIFFERENT page - 'In the example below, Custom 02 is renamed to _Choose Vendor Access Group_ and is used for examples in this document. You have the option of renaming the Custom field in Step 4.' (bcaf1f5a), where Step 4 is Forms and Fields; (c) for the Invoice Routing hierarchy the segments are three invoice HEADER fields, see the compressed range fh.range.custom-10-11-12; (d) fb3e6aa2 calls the same control 'the custom field' rather than Segment Name - 'Select the custom field configured to the selected source list.' - a label drift the driver should expect. The number of Segment Name rows is not free: it must match the source list's level count (bcaf1f5a, 'If a multi-level list was created, be sure to add additional levels and segments to match the list levels.'). [MERGE] Cross-lens duplicate 'segment_name' (procedure and crosscut lenses) carried the identical sourceFile and identical verbatim sourceQuote; folded into this one record under the canonical snake_case name, per refuter 1's direction to prefer these tables-lens notes because they alone carry the documented cardinality rule and the fb3e6aa2 label drift. [HOMONYM GUARD, both refuters] page.accounting-administration ALREADY owns a field named segment_name with label 'Segment Name' and validValues Country / Currency / Custom 1-20 / Org Unit 1-6 / Policy Name, sourced to adding-a-new-segment-d6dfb07b.md on the Account Code Hierarchy for Ledger page. THAT IS A DIFFERENT PAGE AND A DIFFERENT OPTION UNIVERSE. Refuter 2 proved the separation: grep -rln 'Segment Name' over BOTH guide dirs returns exactly two files, d6dfb07b and bcaf1f5a - one per page, zero overlap. DO NOT MERGE THE TWO RECORDS AND DO NOT LET THIS PAGE INHERIT THAT VALUE SET; empty validValues here is the correct blind-build answer. FORMS AND FIELDS BOUNDARY: this record claims only the SELECTION of a field as a segment, never its definition or rename - bcaf1f5a itself defers the rename ('You have the option of renaming the Custom field in Step 4.') to step-4-add-the-custom-field-to-the-employee-form-da376eef.md, which is the BUILT Forms and Fields surface.

fields.label: feature name
fields.sourceQuote: On the Feature Hierarchies, select _Invoice Vendor Employee Access_, and then click Modify Hierarchy.
fields.notes: The selector on the Feature Hierarchies landing screen that picks WHICH named feature hierarchy you are about to edit. validValues is DELIBERATELY EMPTY and that is the correct blind-build answer: NO file in this corpus enumerates the selector's option list. What the corpus gives instead is five feature-hierarchy names each attested in its own separate topic, which is an ATTESTED-NAMES LIST, not a documented option list, and is therefore recorded here in prose rather than promoted into graph values. The five, with their files and verbatim wording: (1) 'Invoice Vendor Employee Access' - 'On the Feature Hierarchies, select _Invoice Vendor Employee Access_, and then click Modify Hierarchy.' (tools-guides/step-2-associate-the-feature-hierarchy-to-the-source-list-bcaf1f5a.md); (2) 'Invoice Payment' - 'Select the Invoice Payment feature name.' (admin-guides/professional-edition-fb3e6aa2.md); (3) 'Invoice Routing' - 'The user first specifies the source list and relevant segments using the Invoice Routing hierarchy in the Feature Hierarchies area.' (tools-guides/create-the-invoice-routing-feature-hierarchy-8b510285.md); (4) 'Payment Authorized Approvers' - '(Optional) Set up the Payment Authorized Approvers hierarchy if you choose to use authorized approvers.' (admin-guides/workflow-creation-process-1d37b85f.md), written elsewhere as 'Authorized Approver Feature Hierarchy' (admin-guides/user-administrator-fcfd570c.md); (5) 'Cost Object Approver' - 'Set up the Cost Object Hierarchy just like any other hierarchy.' (admin-guides/step-1-define-the-cost-object-approver-hierarchy-6e7b7dc6.md). A sixth appears in a workflow context: 'By default, the Request Authorized Approver hierarchy uses the Request and Employee fields' (admin-guides/understand-the-hierarchy-b65d7089.md). WHICH OF THESE A GIVEN SITE ACTUALLY OFFERS IS UNDETERMINED - the list is near-certainly provisioning-dependent, since each name is documented only inside the setup guide for the module that consumes it. An automation driver must match the feature name by text, never by ordinal position. This fan-out across four config domains is the structural reason Feature Hierarchies is a SHARED page and not a Workflows or Routing Configuration surface. [REPAIR APPLIED - HIGHEST-SEVERITY GROUNDING DEFECT ON THIS PAGE] As received from the crosscut lens this record carried validValues ['Invoice Vendor Employee Access','Invoice Payment']. BOTH ARE STRIPPED and validValues is now []. Reasons, both refuters concurring: (a) the record cited bcaf1f5a, where grep -F -c 'Invoice Payment' = 0 - that value lives ONLY in admin-guides/professional-edition-fb3e6aa2.md ('Select the Invoice Payment feature name.', grep -F -c = 1), a different file; (b) the pair was synthesized from two separate single-feature procedures, i.e. two attested instances, not a documented enumeration - exactly the shape the blind-build rule forbids promoting, and the same failure as the two invented 'Yes' values already deleted from this project; (c) it was internally inconsistent, excluding Invoice Routing, Payment Authorized Approvers and Cost Object Approver which have equal footing, so a driver reading two options where the corpus attests five would conclude three real hierarchies do not exist. NO FILE IN THIS CORPUS ENUMERATES THIS SELECTOR'S OPTIONS - 'Feature Hierarchies' appears in 17 files across both guide dirs and not one lists the selector contents. The five attested names are carried in the prose above as an ATTESTED-NAMES LIST, explicitly NON-EXHAUSTIVE and provisioning-dependent. fieldType repaired from the inferred 'dropbox'-style 'dropdown' to 'unknown': the record's own original notes admitted 'the corpus never states the widget', and bcaf1f5a describes selecting a named row on a list page then clicking Modify Hierarchy - the same select-row-then-Modify pattern as page.group-configurations, not an attested dropdown. sourceQuote widened to the full self-contained sentence (grep -F -c = 1 in bcaf1f5a). [DEDUPE] Survivor of a three-way intra-page duplication - feature_name_selector (procedure lens) and featureHierarchyName (tables lens) are the SAME control, same file, same clause, and all three quotes verify verbatim, so neither drop is a grounding refutation. THE REFUTERS SPLIT ON WHICH NAME SURVIVES: refuter 1 chose feature_name_selector, refuter 2 chose feature_name. I took feature_name because both refuters independently held that 'feature name' is the corpus's OWN wording ('Select the Invoice Payment feature name.', fb3e6aa2, grep -F -c = 1) whereas feature_name_selector's label was a describer's paraphrase - '(feature hierarchy row selection on the Feature Hierarchies page)' - which hard-won rule 7 forbids, and its '_selector' suffix is coined; snake_case also matches source_list / level / segment_name on this page. Refuter 1 authorised this outcome in terms: 'If the merge machinery keeps this record instead of the survivor, it MUST be repaired to validValues [] with the attested names carried in notes only, and fieldType set to unknown.' Done. The tables lens's five-name attestation, which refuter 2 ordered transplanted, is the prose above. [SUB-PAGE] This selector sits on the Feature Hierarchies LANDING screen; Source List, Level and Segment Name are reachable only AFTER Modify Hierarchy, and the corpus NEVER NAMES that editor sub-surface - contrast Accounting Administration, where SAP writes 'Select Modify Hierarchy to display the Account Code Hierarchy for Ledger page.' UNNAMED, NOT ABSENT; the graph must not assert a page title for it. A driver must match the feature name by TEXT, never by ordinal position.

GROUNDING. Both refuters ran an exact-substring pass over all 228 lens records and agreed: 228/228 sourceQuotes verbatim, 228/228 cited files present, zero CONCUR_INVOICE/ path regressions. I re-ran that check myself before assembly (228/228) and again on the 114 emitted records after every edit: 114/114 verbatim, 0 path defects, 0 duplicate names. Every quote I hand-authored during repair was grep -F -c'd against its cited file first; all returned 1.

ASSEMBLY METHOD. Records were pulled programmatically out of the three lens JSONs - no quote was retyped. 28 names existed in two lens files under the SAME name; for those I emitted one record (the first lens in the refuters' foundByLenses order, i.e. verbatimVariantIndex 0) and appended the other lens's notes to it verbatim so nothing observed was lost. Two of those variant choices were made against index 0 on explicit refuter instruction: cost_object_hierarchy_type takes the crosscut quote from step-2-activate-the-feature-27a421e2.md because the procedures quote was a value bullet naming no field, and steps_can_be_added_by takes the crosscut record because it is the only one whose cited file enumerates the values.

COUNTS. 96 keeps carried through, 18 routed to repair, 17 of them actually changed; step_email_employee_when_step_is_complete was routed to repair only because the second refuter returned no verdict (a missing verdict routes to Repair, never to deletion) - I re-read work-with-the-steps-page-fab249d1.md, found row 7 sound and its quote verbatim, and changed nothing but the audit note. 86 dropped, every one a duplication drop naming its survivor; NOT ONE control was dropped for failing to be a control, and nothing was dropped for thinness. 114 in, 114 out.

WHAT I REPAIRED, BY CLASS. (a) Six quotes that were verbatim but anchored no control - bare value strings or a truncated NBSP nav fragment - replaced with a field-level sentence from the SAME cited file: expiration_email_to_approver, assignment_timeout_action, restrict_authorized_approver_for, email_notifications_field, allow_employee_to_automatically_transmit_purchase_orders, consolidate_pr_items_same_vendor_into_single_po, plus email_notif_find_workflow_emails_where and step_rule_send_back_message. (b) ONE WRONG-ROW QUOTE, the only defect on this page a grep gate cannot see: workflow_condition_operator_d quoted the E: Data Object row's text. Replaced with the D: Operator row's own line. Note for the builder: columns C and F genuinely share byte-identical row text in the source - that is what the corpus says, not an extractor error. (c) Value-set defects: step_approver_editable_by and step_deletable_by carried the prose article ('the employee' -> 'employee'), with the honest caveat that this enumeration is inline prose the corpus never renders as a list; confirmation_agreement_text had the eight allowed HTML FORMATTING TAGS sitting in validValues, which is markup permitted inside a free-text field and not selectable values - emptied, tags kept in notes with the source's own lower-case '<u>' preserved, 2000-character limit retained as the real constraint. (d) settings_prevent_payment_request_submission_exception_level was the one control whose every available quote carried raw HTML ('...exceeds <cite class="cite">X</cite>'); its label now holds the rendered text and its quote is the same packed cell's description 'Type a number from one to 99.' fromRawHtmlTable stays true. (e) step_rule_exception_visibility kept, fieldType 'unknown', but flagged in notes as a CROSS-SURFACE REFERENCE rather than independent evidence of a third instance - four Audit Rules files define the field, this Workflows file only references it in the Generate Exception context.

WHAT I DELIBERATELY DID NOT DO. (1) NO SPLITS. add-an-email-notification-c237a2de.md documents Email Subject and Email Body twice each, once on the Primary Recipient step and once on the Delegate Recipient step (the delegate body additionally gated by the Use Primary Recipient Email check box) - genuinely two controls apiece. Records created during Repair never face the adversarial refuter, so both stay single records and the splits are reported in splitsProposed for a human. (2) NO RENAMES. One refuter asked for remove_workflow_step -> btn_remove_workflow_step and for email_notif_find_workflow_emails_where -> email_notification_find_workflow_emails_where; both are reasonable family-consistency fixes, but a rename introduces a name the refuters never judged, so both are recorded in the records' notes and here instead. (3) NO RECONCILIATION of the four contradictions this page carries into the graph: the Email Notifications granularity split (one multiselect in 554e86aa vs three per-slot fields in 663bb8ac - both kept); the Steps Can Be Added By value wording (554e86aa's 'the employee and/or the approver' implies an option b847d65b's two-value list omits - list NOT treated as exhaustive); the invoice/payment-request LABEL DRIFT on two Settings-tab controls (general-information-8b3b0308.md says 'Filter invoice items...' and 'Allow processor to recall an invoice...', invoice-settings-cace748d.md says 'payment request' - BOTH forms are kept in notes because a label-matching driver fails against a tenant rendering the other); and the 'Type a number from one to 99.' range in all three settings files against the built Exceptions page's '0 and 99', recorded as a genuine cross-page discrepancy.

NAMING RULE HONOURED. All nine Settings-tab controls are emitted under settings_* and the invoice_settings_* / pr_settings_* / po_settings_* spellings are dropped. Naming any of these 'Invoice Settings' would merge Workflows > Settings tab with the BUILT Invoice Settings page, whose 13 fields come from entirely different files; both refuters re-verified against the 486-field graph that ZERO existing fields cite invoice-settings-cace748d.md, purchase-request-settings-b0bce285.md, purchase-order-settings-a5a997b4.md or conditional-expressions-and-the-condition-page-4d98af34.md. (2) dep.g2ar.025 targets 'Invoice Settings' on a quote naming Workflows and Settings and duplicates dep.g2ar.024. (3) page.exceptions.navPathAlternates contains 'Administration > Invoice > Workflows > Settings', a route to the Settings tab and not to Exceptions. (4) The map phase found the recon's Approval-Statuses sub-tab citation was actually a Delegate Configurations quote; the correct citation is adding-an-invoice-approval-status-d8cbbe5d.md. (5) Two probable G1 gaps found while ruling scope: prevent-approver-from-adding-and-deleting-line-items-in-an-invoice-9de9dba8.md and prevent-processor-to-change-vendor-pending-processor-in-workflow-edbca7d1.md both say explicitly 'On the Invoice Settings page' and are cited by zero graph nodes - report against the BUILT page, do NOT home them on Workflows.

Mine them for structure, names, dates and history claims ONLY. general-information-8b3b0308.md MUST STAY — it is the proof that the settings family sits on the Settings tab. Real payload ~605 table units, not 954. Several tab-level topics are genuine thin stubs and must be recorded as thin rather than padded: workflow-settings-8b3b98e1.md (743 B, content-free section header), reason-category-and-codes-8b3b27d4.md (866 B), confirmation-agreements-8b3aca2e.md (908 B), work-with-invoice-approval-statuses-8b3bab8c.md (922 B). valueSets.context: The complete data-variable catalog that may be typed into an email body. A STRUCTURED catalog, not a picker: every row of the source table yields a LABEL form and a VALUE form of one variable, and the label form is the value form with 'L_' inserted after the opening percent sign.
valueSets.sourceQuote: Field Label: %L\_WhoChanged%
valueSets.notes: ALL 18 DISTINCT VARIABLES, IN SOURCE ORDER, NONE SAMPLED. ESCAPING - A DELIBERATE, FLAGGED TRANSCRIPTION DECISION: the markdown source writes every underscore escaped as backslash-underscore (the sourceQuote above preserves that exactly, which is why it reads '%L\_WhoChanged%'), but the backslash is markdown escaping, not a character of the variable. The values array therefore carries the UNESCAPED strings a user actually types, which is what the automation needs. STRUCTURE: eleven table rows in two labelled sections - 'Invoice or Purchase Request Change' (Changed By, Request Name*, Request Date, Submit Date, Total Amount, Approval Status of the Workflow Step, Pay Status = 7 rows) and 'Invoice or Purchase Request Pending Approval' (Report From, Report From, Request Name, Total = 4 rows). Eleven rows yield 18 rather than 22 distinct variables because %L_RequestName%/%RequestName% and %L_Total%/%Total% appear in BOTH sections; and two different rows share the Field label 'Report From' while carrying DIFFERENT variables (%EmpName% = 'The name of the user who owns the invoice', %SubmittingUserName% = 'The name of the user who submitted the invoice'). The asterisk on 'Request Name*' resolves to the table's own footer row, which the markdown escapes the leading asterisk of: '\*These fields use the configured form field label, if available, instead of the default label.' SEMANTICS from general-information-00eca1ce.md: 'The variables are enclosed in percentage signs, which indicate to the system that they need to be replaced.', 'Adding an “L” (L) and underscore (\_) to the beginning of the variable name tells the system to replace that variable with the field label.', and 'NOTE: If the variable is blank, then both label and value variables will not print in the resulting email.' DO NOT SOURCE THIS CATALOG FROM email-notifications-8b3dbad4.md, which is a 61-row revision history containing exactly one variable.

An exception at or above this level blocks the PO from being transmitted to the vendor once it is created from its purchase request.

dependencies.condition: RESOLUTION SIDE of dep.g2ar.026 (placeholder target 'exception_level_limit'). A validation rule whose action is Exception only flags the line item or allocation; whether that flag actually blocks submission is decided by the Settings-tab threshold on page Workflows.
dependencies.sourceQuote: Exception only: If the rule is triggered, it will flag the line item or line item allocation. Depending on your exception level settings, it may prevent invoice submission.

dependencies.condition: RESOLUTION SIDE of dep.g2ar.021 (placeholder target 'workflow_first_step', which is not a field). The event chosen on a custom audit rule fixes the rule's position relative to the workflow steps built on the Steps page: Payment Post Request Submit fires immediately after the invoice enters the FIRST workflow step, which is why exceptions it raises cannot block submission.
dependencies.sourceQuote: Payment Post Request Submit: The rule is triggered immediately after an invoice enters the first step of workflow. Any exceptions generated will not prevent the invoice from being submitted.

dependencies.condition: RESOLUTION SIDE of dep.g2ar.022 (placeholder target 'workflow_approval_steps', which is not a field). For a RANDOM audit rule the same event name fires at the opposite end of the workflow - after every approval and processor step has completed. CONTRADICTION WORTH KEEPING VISIBLE: the identical event label 'Payment Post Request Submit' is documented with two different firing points, one per rule type, in two different files.
dependencies.sourceQuote: Payment Post Request Submit: The rule is triggered when the invoice has gone through all the approval and processor workflow steps but before the pre-payment validation occurs.

dependencies.condition: GROUP-SCOPED ADMINISTRATION. The Editable By Group(s) control on the Approval Statuses tab selects among group configurations, which are authored on the Group Configurations page. The group must exist there before it can be granted edit rights here.
dependencies.sourceQuote: Select the group configuration(s) that can edit this workflow.

dependencies.condition: INFERRED: the quoted General-page description says 'group rights' without naming the Group Configurations page. The dependency follows from the only documented named option being 'Global Group' and from the sibling Approval Statuses control, whose own description does name group configurations explicitly. A group must exist before it can be selected here.
dependencies.sourceQuote: Select the group rights that an administrator must have in order to modify this workflow.

dependencies.condition: FORWARD REFERENCE, EXPECTED TO STAY UNRESOLVED. Administration > Company > Company Admin > User Administration is out of scope for this graph by the 2026-08-31 decision. Recorded because it is a hard operational consequence: clearing the Settings-tab checkbox activates a centralized approver workflow in which every employee must already have an approver set in User Administration or via the employee import, or submission fails with an error.
dependencies.sourceQuote: every employee must have an approver set for them in the User Administration page or through the employee import.

dependencies.condition: INFERRED: the corpus does not state the ordering in a single sentence; it follows from the two-step procedure whose Step 1 is 'Define the Cost Object Approver Hierarchy' on Feature Hierarchies and whose Step 2 is 'Activate the Feature', where the only control set is Cost Object Hierarchy Type on a workflow's General page. The Step 1 topic also notes the permission boundary - it requires the Feature Hierarchies section, not Workflows.
dependencies.sourceQuote: Set up the Cost Object Hierarchy just like any other hierarchy.

dependencies.condition: THE HARD PREREQUISITE OF THE WHOLE AUTHORIZED-APPROVER SURFACE. The authorized approver hierarchy must be defined on Feature Hierarchies and its source list imported or created BEFORE the Authorized Approver feature can be activated on the Workflows Configuration sub-tab. A driver that opens Workflows > Authorized Approvers first will find the feature unavailable.
dependencies.sourceQuote: You must define the authorized approver hierarchy (Invoice > Feature Hierarchies) and import/create its associated source list before the authorized approver feature can be activated.

dependencies.condition: Second, softer ordering statement from SAP's eight-step workflow creation sequence: setting up the Payment Authorized Approvers hierarchy is step 3, ahead of adding authorized approvers (step 4) and creating the workflow (step 5). CONTRADICTION KEPT, NOT RECONCILED: this file marks the hierarchy step '(Optional)' while understand-the-hierarchy-b65d7089.md states the feature 'cannot be activated' without it. The two are about different things - creating a workflow versus activating the feature - and both stand.
dependencies.sourceQuote: (Optional) Set up the Payment Authorized Approvers hierarchy if you choose to use authorized approvers.

dependencies.condition: FORWARD REFERENCE WITH AN UNRESOLVED FIELD ON A BUILT PAGE. Purchase Request hierarchies - both Authorized Approval and Cost Object Approval - are configured on Feature Hierarchies and only then become selectable through the Policy tool. The built Policies page carries no field for hierarchy selection, so this endpoint is expected to stay unresolved until such a field is added. The quote is deliberately cut before the menu separator: workflow-667cee21.md writes 'Invoice  Feature Hierarchies' with U+00A0 and no '>' glyph, so any quote spanning the arrow fails grep -F.
dependencies.sourceQuote: PR hierarchies are set up independently, including Authorized Approval and COA. These must be configured using Invoice

dependencies.condition: PROVENANCE OF THE SOURCE LIST OPTION SET. The list chosen here must already exist in List Management - it is created and named there in Step 1 and merely selected here in Step 2. This is the resolution side of the pre-existing forward endpoints dep.g5g5.050 and dep.g5g5.051.
dependencies.sourceQuote: In the Source List, select the name of the list you created in Step 1

dependencies.condition: CARDINALITY RULE. The number of Level rows is not free choice: it is dictated by the shape of the list selected in Source List. A multi-level source list forces matching additional levels.
dependencies.sourceQuote: If a multi-level list was created, be sure to add additional levels and segments to match the list levels.

dependencies.condition: Same cardinality rule, second governed control: Segment Name rows are paired one-to-one with Level rows and their count must match the source list's level count.
dependencies.sourceQuote: If a multi-level list was created, be sure to add additional levels and segments to match the list levels.

dependencies.condition: NAVIGATION ORDERING on the Feature Hierarchies landing screen, stated explicitly with 'and then': the named feature hierarchy row is selected FIRST, and only then is Modify Hierarchy clicked. A driver must match the feature name by text, never by ordinal position.
dependencies.sourceQuote: On the Feature Hierarchies, select _Invoice Vendor Employee Access_, and then click Modify Hierarchy.

dependencies.condition: INFERRED: the corpus does not state this ordering in a sentence; it follows from the numbered procedure in professional-edition-fb3e6aa2.md, where 'Select Modify Hierarchy.' is step 3 and 'Select the source list to use to identify the various funding accounts.' is step 4. Modify Hierarchy is the GATE - Source List, Level and Segment Name are unreachable until it is clicked.
dependencies.sourceQuote: Select Modify Hierarchy.

dependencies.condition: The New button inside the Modify Hierarchy editor is what creates a Level row and populates its value. The action is repeatable - one click per hierarchy level required by the source list.
dependencies.sourceQuote: Click New to add Employee as the value for Level (this is the default and cannot be changed).

dependencies.condition: PREREQUISITE DIRECTION. The custom field offered in the Segment Name list must already be configured before the Feature Hierarchies procedure is started. Stated as an explicit precondition note above the numbered steps of the Invoice Payment hierarchy procedure.
dependencies.sourceQuote: The source list and custom field referenced in the steps below must already be configured before you proceed.

The Custom field designated as a segment HERE (Step 2) is afterwards added to the Employee form on Forms and Fields (Step 4), which is what exposes it to end users. The two pages are mutually ordered around one custom field; both edges are real and neither replaces the other.
dependencies.sourceQuote: In this step you will add the field (Custom 02) specified in the Feature Hierarchies step (Step 2) to the Employee form.

dependencies.condition: The Invoice Routing feature hierarchy's source list and segments are specified on Feature Hierarchies, not on Routing Configuration, which then consumes the resulting hierarchy path. DEDUPE NOTE FOR THE MERGER: the pre-existing dep.g2.003 encodes the same relationship from the Routing side with a different quote from the same file, and its source field name 'Source list' differs in case from the roster name 'source_list'; this edge is emitted with the exact roster name so the endpoint resolves. Merge rather than double-count.
dependencies.sourceQuote: The user first specifies the source list and relevant segments using the Invoice Routing hierarchy in the Feature Hierarchies area.

dependencies.condition: FORWARD REFERENCE, EXPECTED TO STAY UNRESOLVED - Administration > Company > Company Admin > User Administration is out of scope for this graph by the 2026-08-31 decision, and the Authorized Approval Limits window is real and documented but is not a page to build. Recorded because the state of THIS page decides which control that window shows: if the Authorized Approver feature is activated and the hierarchy built here has at least one Level in addition to Global, the Authorized Approval Limits link appears; with the Global group alone it does not.
dependencies.sourceQuote: then the Authorized Approval Limits link appears in the Expense and Invoices Setting section

dependencies.condition: FORWARD REFERENCE TO A PAGE THAT IS NOT IN THE GRAPH AND SHOULD STAY UNRESOLVED. The corpus names the surface 'Payment Group Configuration'; it is neither one of the twenty built pages nor one of the named unbuilt ones, and the quote states the requirement without naming a destination page, so the endpoint is deliberately NOT force-bound to Invoice Settings or Group Configurations. The Invoice Payment feature hierarchy must exist before payment groups can be configured.
dependencies.sourceQuote: Feature hierarchy configuration is required before you can configure payment groups.

steps.name: Stand up a new invoice approval workflow end to end (Approval Statuses -> Copy -> General -> Steps -> Step Rules -> Policy)
steps.goal: A brand-new invoice approval workflow exists, is fully stepped and ruled, and is actually in force because a policy points at it. Half-works if a leg is skipped: (a) skip the Approval Statuses tab and the Initial Status list on every step offers only the shipped defaults, so the custom status you meant to drive skip-to-step behaviour with silently does not exist; (b) skip the Copy and there is nothing to configure at all - the corpus states the administrator cannot create a workflow from scratch; (c) build steps but never attach the workflow to a policy and the whole object is inert - nothing routes through it, and worse, once it IS attached it can no longer be deleted; (d) author step rules before the steps exist and the Step Rules page has nothing to attach them to.

sequence.action: on the Approval Statuses tab > Invoice sub-tab, click New and type the name of each custom approval status the workflow will use
sequence.rationale: CORPUS-STATED, and it is literally step 1 of SAP's own ordered list: 'When creating custom invoice workflows, an administrator should perform these steps in the following order:' followed by 'Create any custom approval statuses that you may use in the workflow.' (workflow-creation-process-1d37b85f.md). Run out of order and the Initial Status list on the Add Workflow Step page has no custom entry to offer - work-with-the-steps-page-fab249d1.md states 'You can also create custom approval statuses.' as the source of that list.

sequence.action: type the action text that will become the approver's button label for this status
sequence.rationale: CORPUS-STATED: 'Type descriptive text to be used as the action text. This text becomes button text for the approver.' (adding-an-invoice-approval-status-d8cbbe5d.md). This is the only place the on-screen button label is set; leaving it until after the workflow is built means approvers see an unlabelled or default action for whatever period elapses.

sequence.action: type the description text for the status
sequence.rationale: CORPUS-STATED: 'Type the description text.' (adding-an-invoice-approval-status-d8cbbe5d.md). Ordering is internal to the Request Status window - it must be filled before Save on the same window, not after.

sequence.action: select the group configuration(s) permitted to edit this status, then Save the Request Status window
sequence.rationale: CORPUS-STATED: 'Select the group configuration(s) that can edit this workflow.' (adding-an-invoice-approval-status-d8cbbe5d.md). INFERRED consequence of running it late: this is a rights field, so a status saved with the wrong group is editable by the wrong administrators from the moment it is saved.

sequence.action: on the Workflows tab select the workflow that most closely matches the target and click Copy
sequence.rationale: CORPUS-STATED and non-negotiable: 'To create a new workflow, an administrator must copy an existing invoice workflow and make the appropriate edits.' and 'The administrator cannot create a workflow from scratch.' (create-a-new-workflow-15992497.md). There is no 'New' entry point on the Workflows tab; an automation driver that looks for one stalls. The documented order agrees: 'Create a workflow by copying an existing workflow or the default workflow.' (workflow-creation-process-1d37b85f.md).

sequence.action: on the General page (wizard page 1 of 3) read back Workflow Type and confirm it is the flavour you intended
sequence.rationale: CORPUS-STATED: 'This field is read-only. It identifies the type of workflow that you chose to edit.' (create-a-new-workflow-554e86aa.md). Because it is read-only and inherited from the copy source, order 5 is the ONLY moment the type can be chosen. Discovering the wrong type after the steps are built means discarding the object and copying again.

sequence.action: type a new name for the workflow
sequence.rationale: CORPUS-STATED: 'Type a new name for the workflow. This name does not have to be unique.' (create-a-new-workflow-554e86aa.md). Because names need not be unique, an unrenamed copy is indistinguishable from its source in the Workflows tab list and in the Policies page's workflow list - a driver that assigns by name can bind the policy to the wrong object. Rename before anything selects the workflow by name.

sequence.action: select the group rights an administrator must hold to modify this workflow
sequence.rationale: CORPUS-STATED: 'Select the group rights that an administrator must have in order to modify this workflow.' (create-a-new-workflow-554e86aa.md). CONTRADICTION WORTH DRIVING CAREFULLY: invoice-settings-cace748d.md states that if the Settings-tab own-approver check box is cleared, 'If this check box is not selected, then it overrides the Editable By Group(s) and Steps Can Be Added By fields on the Edit Workflow page and the Add/Edit Workflow Steps page.' - so a value set here can be silently overridden by a control on a different tab, and setting the Settings tab afterwards raises a conflict error.

sequence.action: choose who may add ad hoc steps to this workflow
sequence.rationale: CORPUS-STATED gate on two later General-page fields: 'This field is available only if you have chosen an option in the Steps Can Be Added field.' gates the employee-added-step email option, and 'This field is only available if you have chosen an option in the Steps Can Be Added field field.' (SAP's own duplicated word) gates Restrict Authorized Approver for - both in create-a-new-workflow-554e86aa.md. Leave this empty and those two controls are not merely default, they are absent from the page.

sequence.action: select the action to take when an approver has not approved within the allowed time
sequence.rationale: CORPUS-STATED: 'This setting only appears if the admin has selected an option in the Approval Time Expired field.' (create-a-new-workflow-554e86aa.md) - the day-count field below does not render until this list has a value. The same file gives the OR-gate for the extension field: 'This option is only available if either the Approval Time Expired Action or Assignment Timeout Action options are enabled.'

sequence.action: type the number of days after which the approval expires
sequence.rationale: CORPUS-STATED conditional visibility, the reverse side of order 10: 'This setting only appears if the admin has selected an option in the Approval Time Expired field.' (create-a-new-workflow-554e86aa.md). A driver that tries this field first finds nothing and, if it silently continues, ships a timeout action with no timeout.

sequence.action: click Next to leave the General page
sequence.rationale: CORPUS-STATED wizard transition: 'Click Next.' followed by 'The Steps page appears.' (create-a-new-workflow-554e86aa.md). The Steps page is a wizard page reached only through this button on a workflow already copied - it is not a separate left-menu destination, so there is no way to reach it before orders 5-11 are done.

sequence.action: on the Steps page click New to open the Add Workflow Step window
sequence.rationale: CORPUS-STATED: 'On the Steps page, click New.' (work-with-the-steps-page-fab249d1.md). INFERRED from the wizard structure documented in create-a-new-workflow-554e86aa.md: the Steps page only exists inside the workflow object opened at order 5, so every step created here belongs to that copy and cannot be authored in advance.

sequence.action: type the step name the employee will see on the Approval Flow page
sequence.rationale: CORPUS-STATED: 'Type any alphanumeric name for the workflow step.' (work-with-the-steps-page-fab249d1.md), which also warns the name appears to the employee. INFERRED: naming is first in the window because the remaining fields (Role, Approval Actions) change which controls render, and renaming afterwards means re-opening a saved step.

sequence.action: select the role responsible for completing this step
sequence.rationale: CORPUS-STATED, and the single most order-sensitive control on the Steps page. work-with-the-steps-page-fab249d1.md: 'such as Authorized Approver, Invoice Approver, Invoice Processor, Invoice Processor Manager, or Invoice Vendor Manager' - and if it is a non-system role 'you must select an action or multiple actions in the Approval Actions field.' The same file: 'If you select Authorized Approver, two check boxes appear to select whether or not the authorized approver is based on limit or exception level of the invoice.' Set Role last and the fields you needed were never on screen.

sequence.action: pick the approval actions this approver may take
sequence.rationale: CORPUS-STATED: 'From the Approval Actions helper pane, click an action that an approver can make to an invoice that is awaiting approval.' (work-with-the-steps-page-fab249d1.md). The same file states this field is REQUIRED for any non-system role, and that the control switches between multi-select and single-select depending on the Role chosen at order 15 - so it must follow Role, never precede it.

sequence.action: select who may edit the approver on this step
sequence.rationale: CORPUS-STATED CROSS-TAB GATE: 'If you have the Allow users to select their own approver for payment request field on the Settings page not selected, then the employee does not appear as an option.' (work-with-the-steps-page-fab249d1.md). The employee option is missing from this list entirely unless the Settings tab was set first - so if a centralized workflow is intended, set the Settings tab BEFORE this step, or the value you pick here is later overridden with a conflict error per invoice-settings-cace748d.md.

sequence.action: select who may delete this step from the Approval Flow page
sequence.rationale: CORPUS-STATED: 'Select who can delete this step on the Approval Flow page within Invoice, the employee, approver, or both.' (work-with-the-steps-page-fab249d1.md). INFERRED ordering: this is a per-step right, so it must be set while the step window is open; there is no documented bulk pass to apply it to steps already saved.

sequence.action: select the approval status the invoice takes when this step begins
sequence.rationale: CORPUS-STATED dependency on order 1: 'Click an approval status that represents what the invoice status should be set to when the Step begins, such as Pending Approval.' and, in the same row, 'You can also create custom approval statuses.' (work-with-the-steps-page-fab249d1.md). If the Approval Statuses tab was skipped, this list simply lacks the custom status and the step silently keeps a default - a workflow that looks configured and routes wrongly.

sequence.action: save the step
sequence.rationale: CORPUS-STATED: 'Click Save to return to the Workflows page.' (work-with-the-steps-page-fab249d1.md). INFERRED: the save is what makes the step addressable by the Step Rules page at order 22 - an unsaved step cannot carry a rule.

sequence.action: use the Step Order column to put the saved steps in the intended sequence
sequence.rationale: CORPUS-STATED: 'To place the steps in the proper workflow order, use the Step Order column.' (work-with-the-steps-page-fab249d1.md). HARD ORDERING RULE that must be honoured here and not discovered later: 'The Vendor Approval system step _cannot_ precede the Cost Object Approval step.' (step-3-edit-the-workflow-steps-f2731590.md). ROLE GATE on this action, quoted: 'This portion of the configuration requires permissions for the Workflows section in Administration.' (same file).

sequence.action: on the Step Rules page select a step and click New, then name the rule
sequence.rationale: CORPUS-STATED, and the reason this leg is last: 'Once you have created the workflow steps, you can attach rules to each step.' (work-with-the-step-rules-page-4c33cda0.md). The same file also states 'Not all steps can have rules. If the selected step can have a rule, the New button becomes available.' - so a driver must select a step first and read the New button's state rather than assume every step accepts a rule.

sequence.action: decide whether this rule is always evaluated or only when the other rules on the step are false
sequence.rationale: CORPUS-STATED: 'If the check box is _not_ selected, then the rule is evaluated and executed only if all other rules in this step were determined to be false.' (work-with-the-step-rules-page-4c33cda0.md). INFERRED ordering consequence: because the default behaviour is order-dependent across rules on the same step, adding a second rule later can change whether the first one ever fires - set this deliberately on every rule, not just the first.

sequence.action: in the Edit Action window select the action the rule performs
sequence.rationale: CORPUS-STATED CARDINALITY LIMIT that constrains what can be added afterwards: 'A single workflow rule can contain only one of these actions:' - Skip step, Change approver, Send back to employee (work-with-the-step-rules-page-4c33cda0.md), while Generate an exception and Send email may repeat. A driver that appends a second exclusive action to an existing rule is rejected; it must author a second rule instead.

sequence.action: confirm the condition in the Edit Condition window
sequence.rationale: CORPUS-STATED: 'Click OK.' (edit-workflow-rules-and-actions-abdf9b11.md). INFERRED: the condition is the 'if' half of the rule described in work-with-the-step-rules-page-4c33cda0.md ('Create a condition (the "if" portion...)'), so it must be committed before the action window can be reached and before the rule is meaningful.

sequence.action: click Done to leave the workflow wizard
sequence.rationale: CORPUS-STATED: 'Click Done.' (edit-workflow-properties-409a8f0b.md). INFERRED: Done is the exit from the three-page wizard; until it is clicked the workflow object is still in the editor and the Policies page has nothing new to select.

sequence.action: open the target policy and select the new workflow in the Invoice Workflow list
sequence.rationale: CORPUS-STATED, step 8 of the documented order: 'Assign the invoice workflow to a policy.' (workflow-creation-process-1d37b85f.md), reinforced by 'Once you have created the workflow, you must associate it to a policy.' (create-a-new-workflow-15992497.md). Skip this and the workflow exists but nothing routes through it. LABEL DRIFT TO EXPECT: activating-the-confirmation-agreement-feature-bdfc1dce.md describes this same list as 'In the Expense Report Workflow list, choose the appropriate workflow.' - two different labels in the corpus for the same association.

sequence.action: save the policy
sequence.rationale: CORPUS-STATED: 'Click Save.' (activating-the-confirmation-agreement-feature-bdfc1dce.md, policy association procedure). ONE-WAY DOOR the operator should know before saving: 'The system does not allow you to delete a workflow that is currently assigned to a policy.' (delete-a-workflow-or-workflow-steps-e9a84a07.md) - after this save, removing the workflow requires unassigning it here first.

steps.name: Configure the Authorized Approver feature (hierarchy first, then activation, then steps, then the approver list)
steps.goal: Invoices route to approvers whose authority is bounded by an approval limit and/or an exception range, driven by a real hierarchy. The corpus makes the ordering a hard blocker rather than a preference: without the Feature Hierarchies leg the feature cannot even be activated; without activation the ad hoc restriction options are absent from the workflow; without a step whose Role is Authorized Approver the feature is inert; and without a level on that step the Level field never appears on the approver record, so every approver ends up unlevelled and the filtering silently does nothing.

sequence.action: create the list that will back the Authorized Approver hierarchy and give it a descriptive name
sequence.rationale: CORPUS-STATED HARD BLOCKER: 'and import/create its associated source list before the authorized approver feature can be activated.' (understand-the-hierarchy-b65d7089.md). The Global-group-vs-hierarchy matrix states the same requirement as step 1 of the hierarchy column: 'Create a connected (multi-level) list of the hierarchy levels.' (global-group-vs-authorized-approver-hierarchy-8a960238.md). A driver that opens Workflows first finds the feature unactivatable.

sequence.action: add each list item's code
sequence.rationale: CORPUS-STATED, and the reason codes must be settled before anything downstream reads them: 'The code format (EAST; NORTH) for each list item must be typed exactly as you have entered them here in your import.' (step-1-create-the-source-list-in-list-management-cc91aa73.md). Changing a code after the hierarchy and any import reference it breaks the match silently.

sequence.action: add each list item's display name
sequence.rationale: CORPUS-STATED: the source list items are what the hierarchy levels resolve to - 'The source list is the hierarchical structure that will become the named vendor groups to which vendors will be assigned.' (step-1-create-the-source-list-in-list-management-cc91aa73.md, describing the same list-building procedure). INFERRED: names are cosmetic where codes are load-bearing, so they may be edited later without breaking the match - unlike order 2.

sequence.action: add sub-levels if the hierarchy is to be multi-level, then click Done
sequence.rationale: CORPUS-STATED: 'Create a connected (multi-level) list of the hierarchy levels.' (global-group-vs-authorized-approver-hierarchy-8a960238.md) and, from the parallel vendor-access procedure, 'If a multi-level list was created, be sure to add additional levels and segments to match the list levels.' (step-2-associate-the-feature-hierarchy-to-the-source-list-bcaf1f5a.md). Depth added after the hierarchy is mapped leaves hierarchy levels and list levels out of step.

sequence.action: click Done to close out the list
sequence.rationale: INFERRED from the list-building procedure in step-1-create-the-source-list-in-list-management-cc91aa73.md, which ends the item loop with 'Click Done when all list items have been added.' The list must be complete and closed before it can be picked as a Source List on Feature Hierarchies.

sequence.action: select the Invoice Authorized Approver feature hierarchy from the landing screen
sequence.rationale: CORPUS-STATED: the hierarchy is defined here and nowhere else - 'You must define the authorized approver hierarchy (Invoice' ... 'Feature Hierarchies)' per understand-the-hierarchy-b65d7089.md (quote continues 'and import/create its associated source list before the authorized approver feature can be activated.'). The workflow-creation order names the same leg: '(Optional) Set up the Payment Authorized Approvers hierarchy if you choose to use authorized approvers.' (workflow-creation-process-1d37b85f.md) - optional only because authorized approvers themselves are optional, not because the ordering is.

sequence.action: click Modify Hierarchy to open the detail editor
sequence.rationale: CORPUS-STATED: 'Select Modify Hierarchy.' (professional-edition-fb3e6aa2.md). ROLE GATE, quoted: 'This portion of the configuration requires permissions for the Feature Hierarchies section in Administration.' (step-1-define-the-cost-object-approver-hierarchy-6e7b7dc6.md) - a Workflows-only administrator cannot complete this leg at all.

sequence.action: select the list built in orders 1-5 as the Source List
sequence.rationale: CORPUS-STATED, and the resolution of the prerequisite: 'In the Source List, select the name of the list you created in Step 1' (step-2-associate-the-feature-hierarchy-to-the-source-list-bcaf1f5a.md). The corpus is explicit that the list must pre-exist: 'The source list and custom field referenced in the steps below must already be configured before you proceed.' (professional-edition-fb3e6aa2.md).

sequence.action: click New to add a level row
sequence.rationale: CORPUS-STATED: 'Click New to add Employee as the value for Level (this is the default and cannot be changed).' (step-2-associate-the-feature-hierarchy-to-the-source-list-bcaf1f5a.md). INFERRED: level rows and segment rows are paired one-to-one, so a level must be created before a segment can be assigned to it.

sequence.action: set the level for the row
sequence.rationale: CORPUS-STATED, AND THE CORPUS CONTRADICTS ITSELF HERE - recorded rather than reconciled: step-2-associate-the-feature-hierarchy-to-the-source-list-bcaf1f5a.md says of the Vendor Employee Access hierarchy 'Click New to add Employee as the value for Level (this is the default and cannot be changed).', while professional-edition-fb3e6aa2.md instructs 'Set the level to Request.' for the Invoice Payment hierarchy. The corpus gives different level behaviour per feature hierarchy; do not assume either is universal. CONSEQUENCE OF LEVEL COUNT, corpus-stated in the same family: whether the hierarchy carries at least one level beyond Global determines which control User Administration later exposes.

sequence.action: select the field that acts as the hierarchy path segment for this level
sequence.rationale: CORPUS-STATED: 'In the Segment Name list, select the field that will act as the list in User Permissions' (step-2-associate-the-feature-hierarchy-to-the-source-list-bcaf1f5a.md). The field must already exist and already be tied to the source list - 'The source list and custom field referenced in the steps below must already be configured before you proceed.' (professional-edition-fb3e6aa2.md) - so a segment chosen before the field is configured resolves to nothing.

sequence.action: click Save to commit the hierarchy
sequence.rationale: CORPUS-STATED: 'Click Save.' (step-2-associate-the-feature-hierarchy-to-the-source-list-bcaf1f5a.md). This save is the boundary the Workflows leg depends on: only after it does the activation gate in order 13 become satisfiable.

sequence.action: on the Authorized Approvers tab > Configuration sub-tab, select the feature activation check box
sequence.rationale: CORPUS-STATED: 'To activate the feature, select Authorized Approver feature is available for workflows.' (procedure-2d20b513.md), and this is step 2 of the two-column configuration matrix in global-group-vs-authorized-approver-hierarchy-8a960238.md (required for BOTH the global-group-only path and the hierarchy path). (global-group-vs-authorized-approver-hierarchy-8a960238.md). sequence.rationale: CORPUS-STATED: 'Select Restrict approvers to those with exception authority to limit the type of authorized approver.' (create-an-authorized-approver-step-4640b5a5.md). Run this before orders 6-12 and the left-hand tree has no groups to select, so 'Select the group that is associated this authorized approver.' (same file) cannot be performed. (create-a-new-workflow-554e86aa.md - SAP's duplicated word preserved). Without a value here the ad hoc restriction control does not render.
