sequence.action: assign authorized approver rights to users as an alternative or supplement to the Authorized Approver List
sequence.rationale: CORPUS-STATED alternative path, recorded as a FORWARD REFERENCE THAT STAYS UNRESOLVED: step-4-assign-the-proper-rights-to-users-86389a18.md lists three routes and states 'Regardless of how the authorized approvers are entered into Invoice, they all appear in the Authorized Approver List.' - so this leg is interchangeable with orders 22-25, not additional to them. The destination is Administration > Company > Company Admin > User Administration, which is OUT OF SCOPE for this graph by the 2026-08-31 decision; no page node exists and none should be created.

steps.name: Build a Vendor Employee Access hierarchy across the six tools in SAP's stated order
steps.goal: Vendors are partitioned into named groups and each employee can be pointed at exactly one group, so an invoice user only sees their own vendors. This is the procedure the corpus most explicitly orders, and every leg is load-bearing: the list supplies the codes, the hierarchy binds a custom field to those codes, Group Configurations creates groups whose names must match the list levels, and Forms and Fields is what EXPOSES the custom field on the Employee form. Skip the Forms and Fields leg and the whole chain is invisible - the User Administrator has no field to pick the vendor group from, so the hierarchy exists and nothing uses it.

sequence.action: create the source list and name it
sequence.rationale: CORPUS-STATED, step 1 of an explicitly ordered six-tool sequence: 'The administrator uses the following tools in the order presented to configure the feature.' - List Management, Feature Hierarchies, Group Configurations, Forms and Fields, Vendor Employee Access Import, User Administration (overview-of-steps-37e3c289.md). ROLE GATE, quoted from the same sentence: 'All tasks require the Invoice Configuration administrator role unless' (noted otherwise).

sequence.action: add each list item's code, recording it exactly
sequence.rationale: CORPUS-STATED and the single most brittle value in this procedure: 'The code format (EAST; NORTH) for each list item must be typed exactly as you have entered them here in your import.' (step-1-create-the-source-list-in-list-management-cc91aa73.md). The Vendor Employee Access import at tool 5 matches on these codes; changing one afterwards breaks the mapping with no error at configuration time.

sequence.action: add each list item's name - these become the named vendor groups
sequence.rationale: CORPUS-STATED: 'The source list is the hierarchical structure that will become the named vendor groups to which vendors will be assigned.' (step-1-create-the-source-list-in-list-management-cc91aa73.md). Order 6 depends directly on these names: 'In this step you will create groups that match the source list levels you created in Step 1 and matched to the feature hierarchy in Step 2.' (step-3-set-up-the-named-vendor-groups-in-group-configurations-abf369db.md).

sequence.action: add sub-levels now if multi-level vendor groups are intended
sequence.rationale: CORPUS-STATED: 'If a multi-level list was created, be sure to add additional levels and segments to match the list levels.' (step-2-associate-the-feature-hierarchy-to-the-source-list-bcaf1f5a.md). Depth decided here propagates into the hierarchy segments (order 9), the group tree (order 7) and the Connected Lists tab (order 14); adding it later means revisiting all four.

sequence.action: click Done to close the list
sequence.rationale: INFERRED from the list procedure's own closing instruction, 'Click Done when all list items have been added.' (step-1-create-the-source-list-in-list-management-cc91aa73.md). A list left open is not selectable as a Source List on the next page.

sequence.action: select the Invoice Vendor Employee Access feature hierarchy and click Modify Hierarchy
sequence.rationale: CORPUS-STATED, step 2 of the six-tool order: 'On the Feature Hierarchies, select _Invoice Vendor Employee Access_, and then click Modify Hierarchy.' and 'In this step you will associate the source list you created in Step 1' (step-2-associate-the-feature-hierarchy-to-the-source-list-bcaf1f5a.md). The page is a sibling left-menu tool, not a sub-page of List Management: 'Click List Management (left menu).' appears in step-1-create-the-source-list-in-list-management-cc91aa73.md and 'Click Feature Hierarchies (left menu).' in step-2-associate-the-feature-hierarchy-to-the-source-list-bcaf1f5a.md.

sequence.action: click Modify Hierarchy to open the editor
sequence.rationale: CORPUS-STATED: 'Select Modify Hierarchy.' (professional-edition-fb3e6aa2.md). INFERRED: the Source List, Level and Segment Name controls live inside this editor, so nothing on this page can be configured from the landing screen alone.

sequence.action: pick the list created at order 1 in Source List
sequence.rationale: CORPUS-STATED: 'In the Source List, select the name of the list you created in Step 1' (step-2-associate-the-feature-hierarchy-to-the-source-list-bcaf1f5a.md). This is exactly why List Management is step 1 and not step 2 - the list must be selectable before the hierarchy can bind to it.

sequence.action: click New to add a level row
sequence.rationale: CORPUS-STATED: 'Click New to add Employee as the value for Level (this is the default and cannot be changed).' (step-2-associate-the-feature-hierarchy-to-the-source-list-bcaf1f5a.md). The row must exist before a segment can be attached to it.

sequence.action: accept Employee as the level for this hierarchy
sequence.rationale: CORPUS-STATED, and explicitly not a choice on this hierarchy: 'Click New to add Employee as the value for Level (this is the default and cannot be changed).' (step-2-associate-the-feature-hierarchy-to-the-source-list-bcaf1f5a.md). CONTRADICTION ACROSS FEATURE HIERARCHIES, recorded not reconciled: professional-edition-fb3e6aa2.md instructs 'Set the level to Request.' for the Invoice Payment hierarchy - so a driver must not carry either level value across hierarchies.

sequence.action: select the custom field that will act as the segment (the corpus example uses Custom 02)
sequence.rationale: CORPUS-STATED, and the field named HERE is the one exposed at order 13: 'In this step you will add the field (Custom 02) specified in the Feature Hierarchies step (Step 2) to the Employee form.' (step-4-add-the-custom-field-to-the-employee-form-da376eef.md). Choose a different field on the form than the one named here and the two ends of the chain never meet.

sequence.action: click Save
sequence.rationale: CORPUS-STATED: 'Click Save.' (step-2-associate-the-feature-hierarchy-to-the-source-list-bcaf1f5a.md). INFERRED: the hierarchy must be committed before the group names created at order 13 can be checked against the list levels it maps.

sequence.action: open the Vendor Access tab
sequence.rationale: CORPUS-STATED, step 3 of the six-tool order: 'Click the Vendor Access tab.' within 'In this step you will create groups that match the source list levels you created in Step 1 and matched to the feature hierarchy in Step 2.' (step-3-set-up-the-named-vendor-groups-in-group-configurations-abf369db.md). Both prior legs must be finished because this step is defined by matching them.

sequence.action: click New to open the Select Group window
sequence.rationale: CORPUS-STATED: the procedure at step-3-set-up-the-named-vendor-groups-in-group-configurations-abf369db.md runs 'Click New to open the Select Group window.' INFERRED: the Global tree it opens is only meaningful once the hierarchy from orders 6-12 exists.

sequence.action: open the Global list, select the group name at its level and click Done
sequence.rationale: CORPUS-STATED, including the multi-level case: 'Multi-level list: To select a sub-group, open the list further and select the group name at its level, then click Done.' (step-3-set-up-the-named-vendor-groups-in-group-configurations-abf369db.md). The depth available here is the depth created at order 4 - which is why sub-levels cannot be deferred.

sequence.action: type the vendor group name and Save, repeating until the named groups match the source list items
sequence.rationale: CORPUS-STATED naming constraint that only bites at this point in the order: 'In this instance, the name does not need to match any existing code and may be descriptive. It cannot be the name of any existing group name already in the system.' (step-3-set-up-the-named-vendor-groups-in-group-configurations-abf369db.md). The same step requires 'repeating until the named groups match those you created for your source list in Step 1' - a mismatch here is the classic silent half-configuration.

sequence.action: set Form Type to Employee
sequence.rationale: CORPUS-STATED, step 4 of the six-tool order: 'In Form Type, select Employee.' (step-4-add-the-custom-field-to-the-employee-form-da376eef.md). This is the leg whose omission makes the whole chain invisible - the same file states the purpose plainly: 'Doing this allows this field to be exposed in the User Administration' (Expense and Invoice Settings page).

sequence.action: select the form under Form Name on the Forms tab
sequence.rationale: CORPUS-STATED: 'In the Forms tab, first select the form under Form Name, then click Add Fields.' (step-4-add-the-custom-field-to-the-employee-form-da376eef.md). The corpus states the selection order explicitly in that one sentence - form first, Add Fields second - so a driver that clicks Add Fields with no form selected has nothing to add to.

sequence.action: click Add Fields
sequence.rationale: CORPUS-STATED, same sentence as order 18: 'first select the form under Form Name, then click Add Fields.' (step-4-add-the-custom-field-to-the-employee-form-da376eef.md).

sequence.action: select the custom field named at order 11 in the Add Fields to Forms selector
sequence.rationale: CORPUS-STATED: 'In Add Fields to Forms, select a field (Custom 02 in example below) and click Add Fields, repeating the process if multiple levels are to be added.' (step-4-add-the-custom-field-to-the-employee-form-da376eef.md). It must be the SAME field chosen as the hierarchy segment - the file ties the two steps together explicitly ('the field (Custom 02) specified in the Feature Hierarchies step (Step 2)').

sequence.action: confirm the addition
sequence.rationale: CORPUS-STATED: the same instruction ends 'and click Add Fields, repeating the process if multiple levels are to be added.' (step-4-add-the-custom-field-to-the-employee-form-da376eef.md). INFERRED: the repetition count is set by the level depth chosen at order 4 - one field per level.

sequence.action: optionally rename the field on the Form Fields tab so users see a meaningful label
sequence.rationale: CORPUS-STATED and explicitly optional, but the corpus flags that its example depends on it: 'In the example below, Custom 02 is renamed to _Choose Vendor Access Group_ and is used for examples in this document. You have the option of renaming the Custom field in Step 4.' (step-2-associate-the-feature-hierarchy-to-the-source-list-bcaf1f5a.md). INFERRED ordering: rename AFTER adding, since the rename acts on a field already on the form.

sequence.action: if the vendor groups are multi-level, configure the fields on the Connected Lists tab
sequence.rationale: CORPUS-STATED and conditional on order 4: 'Use the Connected Lists tab if you have created a multi-level vendor group list' and '(Optional): If creating a multi-level list, click the Connected Lists tab and configure your fields by first selecting the list, then following the steps.' (step-4-add-the-custom-field-to-the-employee-form-da376eef.md). Skip it on a multi-level list and the second and third fields do not filter from the first.

sequence.action: select the named vendor group for the user using the newly added field
sequence.rationale: CORPUS-STATED as step 6 of the ordered tool list, but recorded as a FORWARD REFERENCE THAT STAYS UNRESOLVED: 'The User Administrator accesses User Administration and uses the newly-added field in Step 6 to select the named vendor group' (overview-of-steps-37e3c289.md). The same source flags this as the one tool NOT covered by the Invoice Configuration administrator role. Administration > Company surfaces are out of scope for this graph, so no page node exists for it.

steps.name: Author a workflow email notification on its tab, then select it on the workflow's General page
steps.goal: Approvers and submitters receive a customised notification rather than the shipped default. Two things half-work if the order is broken: authoring a notification and never selecting it on a workflow means it is inert (the corpus is explicit that assignment happens on a different tab); and selecting a notification before authoring one means the General-page lists offer only the stock entries. A third, non-configurable dependency exists downstream: whatever is set here, delivery still depends on the recipient's own Profile setting.

sequence.action: on the Email Notifications tab, filter the list to Payment Requests Notifications or Purchase Request Notifications and select a notification to copy
sequence.rationale: CORPUS-STATED, and the reason a copy is the only entry point: 'Add a new email notification by copying an existing notification, then editing the copy.' (add-an-email-notification-c237a2de.md), reached via 'in the Find workflow emails where list, select Payment Requests Notifications or Purchase Request Notifications.' (same file). A driver looking for a 'New' button on this tab finds none.

sequence.action: on the General step of the Modify Email Notification window, set the notification name
sequence.rationale: CORPUS-STATED HARD LIMIT ON THE FRESH COPY: 'The only fields that can be edited at this time are Email Notification Name and Display as From.' (add-an-email-notification-c237a2de.md). Everything else on the General step is locked until the copy is saved and reopened - the same file says 'If you need to make changes to the other fields, save this copy and then edit it as detailed in Modifying an Email Notification in this guide.' This name is also what appears in the workflow's notification lists at orders 8-11 (modify-an-email-notification-a6e5f4ba.md: 'This name will appear in the email notification list while editing the workflow.'), so an unrenamed copy is unpickable.

sequence.action: set the from-address recipients will see
sequence.rationale: CORPUS-STATED: 'Type the email address you would like the recipient to see when they receive the notification.' (modify-an-email-notification-a6e5f4ba.md), and it is the second of only two fields editable on the fresh copy per add-an-email-notification-c237a2de.md. Miss it in this window and it requires a second save-and-reopen pass.

sequence.action: click Next to move to the Primary Recipient step
sequence.rationale: CORPUS-STATED wizard transition within the Modify Email Notification window - the procedure at add-an-email-notification-c237a2de.md runs General -> Primary Recipient -> Delegate Recipient via Next. INFERRED: the Subject and Body controls are per wizard step, so a driver must traverse the steps rather than expecting one flat form.

sequence.action: edit the Email Subject on the Primary Recipient step
sequence.rationale: CORPUS-STATED: 'Make the desired changes to the Email Subject field.' (add-an-email-notification-c237a2de.md). SPLIT WARNING FOR AN AUTOMATION DRIVER: the same file documents this field TWICE, once on the Primary Recipient step and once on the Delegate Recipient step. Filling the primary subject does NOT fill the delegate subject; they are two controls sharing one label and must be addressed separately.

sequence.action: edit the Email Body on the Primary Recipient step
sequence.rationale: CORPUS-STATED: 'Make the desired changes to the Email Body field.' (add-an-email-notification-c237a2de.md). Same two-instance caveat as order 5. INFERRED: the body must be authored before the delegate decision at order 7, because that decision is whether to reuse THIS body.

sequence.action: on the Delegate Recipient step, either tick Use Primary Recipient Email or author a separate delegate body
sequence.rationale: CORPUS-STATED: 'If you want the primary recipient email and the delegate email to be the same, select (enable) the Use Primary Recipient Email check box.' (add-an-email-notification-c237a2de.md). This is the one place the two-instance split can be collapsed; leave it clear and skip the delegate body and delegates receive the unedited stock text while the primary text looks correct.

sequence.action: decide whether the new text overwrites every language
sequence.rationale: CORPUS-STATED: 'Select Yes if you would like to apply the new text to all languages.' (modify-an-email-notification-a6e5f4ba.md). ORDER MATTERS BECAUSE IT IS DESTRUCTIVE ACROSS LOCALES - set it before saving edited text, since applying to all languages after per-language work has been done overwrites that work.

sequence.action: click Done to finish the notification
sequence.rationale: CORPUS-STATED: the notification procedure ends 'Click Done.' (add-an-email-notification-c237a2de.md). INFERRED: until the notification is committed it does not appear in the workflow General-page lists at orders 10-12.

sequence.action: open the workflow's General page and select the notification sent to the approver on submission
sequence.rationale: CORPUS-STATED CROSS-TAB ORDERING, the crux of this whole procedure: 'Once the email notification is configured, the administrator assigns it to a workflow on the Workflows tab.' (overview-8b3df67d.md). The field itself: 'This notification is sent to the approver when the invoice is submitted by the employee.' (select-an-email-notification-in-the-workflows-tab-663bb8ac.md). Author-then-assign; a notification never assigned here never sends.

sequence.action: select the status-change notification
sequence.rationale: CORPUS-STATED: 'This notification is sent to the submitter when the workflow status of the invoice changes.' (select-an-email-notification-in-the-workflows-tab-663bb8ac.md). Same author-then-assign ordering as order 10. CONTRADICTION IN THE CORPUS, carried not resolved: create-a-new-workflow-554e86aa.md presents Email Notifications as one General-page control, while 663bb8ac presents three separate per-slot selectors - a driver should expect either rendering.

sequence.action: select the sent-back notification
sequence.rationale: CORPUS-STATED: 'This notification is sent to the submitter when the invoice is sent back to them.' (select-an-email-notification-in-the-workflows-tab-663bb8ac.md). NOTE recorded on this field in the roster: this notification is always sent and is not configurable on/off - only WHICH template is used is configurable here.

sequence.action: select the template used when an approval times out
sequence.rationale: CORPUS-STATED: 'When the time for approving an invoice has expired, the system can send out an expiration email to the approver' (create-a-new-workflow-554e86aa.md), and add-an-email-notification-c237a2de.md states these copies exist precisely for this slot - 'These email notifications appear for use in Workflows when selecting an optional email notification template to send to an approver when a workflow step has timed out.' DEPENDS ON THE TIMEOUT LEG: with no Approval Time Expired Action set (grpworkflows-s1, order 10) there is no timeout to email about.

steps.name: Set the three exception-level thresholds on the Workflows Settings tab (invoice, purchase request, purchase order)
steps.goal: Documents carrying a severe enough exception are stopped before they move - an invoice cannot be submitted, a purchase request cannot be submitted, a purchase order cannot be transmitted. The threshold is a bare number and means nothing on its own: the exceptions and their levels must already exist, or the number blocks nothing and the configuration looks complete while being inert. Note that these three controls sit on three separate settings tables of the SAME Settings tab of the Workflows page - they are NOT the already-built 'Invoice Settings' page.

sequence.action: create the exception and give it a code, then set its level
sequence.rationale: CORPUS-STATED, and the Exceptions page's own documentation points forward at this very procedure: 'A workflow setting exists that prevents an invoice from being submitted if it has an exception of a certain level.' (add-exceptions-7b73d8f0.md). The level is defined here - 'Type any number between 0 and 99.' (same file). Set the Workflows threshold first and there is no exception at or above it, so nothing is ever blocked.

sequence.action: attach the exception to the rule that will raise it, confirming the level it carries
sequence.rationale: INFERRED from the direction of the reference, not stated as a numbered sequence: an exception blocks submission only when something raises it, and the Audit Rules editor is where a defined exception is bound to a rule - 'It appears in the Exception Code, Exception Level, and Exception Text fields at the top of the page.' (add-a-custom-audit-rule-0f1d320e.md), i.e. the rule editor echoes the level defined at order 1. Skip this and the threshold is armed against an exception nothing ever generates.

sequence.action: on the Settings tab, invoice settings table, type the level above which an invoice cannot be submitted
sequence.rationale: CORPUS-STATED: 'Type a number from one to 99. Any invoice that meets the criteria for an exception with this level or above prevents the employee from submitting the invoice.' (invoice-settings-cace748d.md, a packed raw <table> row - a markdown-only parse misses it). CROSS-PAGE CONTRADICTION, recorded not reconciled: this file's range is 'one to 99' while the Exceptions page that defines the levels says 'Type any number between 0 and 99.' (add-exceptions-7b73d8f0.md). A level-0 exception can therefore be defined that this threshold cannot be set to match.

sequence.action: on the Settings tab, purchase request settings table, type the level above which a PR cannot be submitted
sequence.rationale: CORPUS-STATED, and it is a genuinely separate control rather than the same one relabelled: 'Type a number from one to 99. Any purchase request that meets the criteria for an exception with this level or above prevents the employee from submitting the PR.' (purchase-request-settings-b0bce285.md). Setting only the invoice threshold leaves purchase requests unblocked - the classic half-configuration this step exists to prevent.

sequence.action: on the Settings tab, purchase order settings table, type the level above which a PO cannot be transmitted
sequence.rationale: CORPUS-STATED, and note the different verb - this one gates TRANSMISSION, not submission: 'Type a number from one to 99. Any purchase order that meets the criteria for an exception with this level or above prevents the PO from being transmitted once it is created from its associated purchase request (PR).' (purchase-order-settings-a5a997b4.md). It fires later in the lifecycle than orders 3-4, so a PR that passed its own threshold can still stall here.

sequence.action: click Save on the Workflow Settings page
sequence.rationale: CORPUS-STATED, with an explicit warning about immediacy: 'On the Workflow Settings page, select a setting option.' then Save, after which 'The system applies the setting immediately.' (enabling-and-disabling-an-invoice-workflow-setting-0e1e6d33.md). There is no staging - a threshold saved before the exceptions at orders 1-2 exist takes effect at once and blocks nothing, and a wrong number blocks live traffic the moment it is saved.

steps.name: Configure Cost Object Approval (hierarchy, then the workflow's Cost Object Hierarchy Type, then step order and self-approval)
steps.goal: Invoices route to the approver who owns the cost object they are charged to. The corpus orders this as define-hierarchy then activate-on-workflow then edit-steps, and each leg fails quietly on its own: the Cost Object Hierarchy Type list has nothing coherent to resolve without the hierarchy; the step order can violate a documented hard rule; and Allow Self Cost Object Approval is a check box that can be ticked with no effect at all unless Allow Self Approval is also on. Note the two legs sit behind DIFFERENT permissions.

sequence.action: select the Cost Object Approver hierarchy
sequence.rationale: CORPUS-STATED as step 1 of the Cost Object Approval configuration, and explicitly generic: 'Set up the Cost Object Hierarchy just like any other hierarchy.' (step-1-define-the-cost-object-approver-hierarchy-6e7b7dc6.md) - SAP publishes no COA-specific hierarchy procedure, so the generic Feature Hierarchies flow applies. ROLE GATE, quoted from the same file: 'This portion of the configuration requires permissions for the Feature Hierarchies section in Administration.'

sequence.action: click Modify Hierarchy
sequence.rationale: CORPUS-STATED: 'Select Modify Hierarchy.' (professional-edition-fb3e6aa2.md), the generic editor entry point that step-1-define-the-cost-object-approver-hierarchy-6e7b7dc6.md defers to with 'Set up the Cost Object Hierarchy just like any other hierarchy.'

sequence.action: select the source list backing the cost object structure
sequence.rationale: CORPUS-STATED prerequisite carried by the generic procedure: 'The source list and custom field referenced in the steps below must already be configured before you proceed.' (professional-edition-fb3e6aa2.md). The list is built in List Management, which is why that page precedes Feature Hierarchies in SAP's stated tool order (overview-of-steps-37e3c289.md).

sequence.action: add the level rows
sequence.rationale: INFERRED from the generic instruction 'Set up the Cost Object Hierarchy just like any other hierarchy.' (step-1-define-the-cost-object-approver-hierarchy-6e7b7dc6.md) combined with the two documented level behaviours - Employee, fixed, for Vendor Employee Access (step-2-associate-the-feature-hierarchy-to-the-source-list-bcaf1f5a.md) and Request for Invoice Payment (professional-edition-fb3e6aa2.md). THE CORPUS DOES NOT STATE WHICH LEVEL VALUE THE COA HIERARCHY TAKES; do not assume either.

sequence.action: select the field acting as each hierarchy path segment
sequence.rationale: CORPUS-STATED for the generic editor: 'In the Segment Name list, select the field that will act as the list in User Permissions' (step-2-associate-the-feature-hierarchy-to-the-source-list-bcaf1f5a.md). INFERRED for COA specifically, via 'Set up the Cost Object Hierarchy just like any other hierarchy.' (step-1-define-the-cost-object-approver-hierarchy-6e7b7dc6.md) - the segments are what an invoice's cost object values are matched against, so a hierarchy with no segments resolves no approver.

sequence.action: click Save
sequence.rationale: CORPUS-STATED: 'Click Save.' (step-2-associate-the-feature-hierarchy-to-the-source-list-bcaf1f5a.md). This save is the boundary: order 7 is titled 'Step 2: Activate the Feature' precisely because the hierarchy is Step 1.

sequence.action: from the Invoice Processing Admin menu open Workflows, then select the workflow and click Modify (or Copy to create a new one)
sequence.rationale: CORPUS-STATED: 'Modify an existing workflow by selecting it and clicking Modify (or double-click the desired workflow).' (step-2-activate-the-feature-27a421e2.md). ROLE GATE, quoted from the same file and DIFFERENT from order 1's: 'This portion of the configuration requires permissions for the Workflows section in Administration.' - one operator may be able to do the hierarchy leg and not this one.

sequence.action: on the General page set the Cost Object Hierarchy Type
sequence.rationale: CORPUS-STATED: 'In the Cost Object Hierarchy Type field, select the desired type: Level or Limit.' (step-2-activate-the-feature-27a421e2.md), which is the topic SAP titles 'Step 2: Activate the Feature' - the activation is this field, not a separate switch. The same file adds the conditional follow-on: '(Optional) If Limit is selected, you can also select Cost Object Hierarchy Type to route the cost object _directly_ to that approver with the required approval limit amount.'

sequence.action: click Next to reach the Steps page
sequence.rationale: CORPUS-STATED: 'Click Next. The Steps page appears (see next section).' (step-2-activate-the-feature-27a421e2.md). The Steps page is reachable only through the wizard on an opened workflow, so the General-page value at order 8 is necessarily committed first.

sequence.action: reorder the workflow steps so the Cost Object Approval step sits correctly
sequence.rationale: CORPUS-STATED HARD RULE, and the one thing in this procedure that produces an invalid workflow rather than an inert one: 'The Vendor Approval system step _cannot_ precede the Cost Object Approval step.' (step-3-edit-the-workflow-steps-f2731590.md). The same file gives the default placement to reason from: 'By default, the new workflow step appears in the workflow just prior to the Prepayment Validation step.'

sequence.action: on the General page enable Allow Self Approval
sequence.rationale: CORPUS-STATED MASTER GATE that must precede order 12: 'This feature will only work if the Allow Self Approval option is also selected (enabled).' (create-a-new-workflow-554e86aa.md, of Allow Self Cost Object Approval). Tick the cost-object option alone and it is saved, displayed as on, and does nothing - the textbook silent half-configuration. The same file gates a second control the same way: 'The Allow Self Approval option must be enabled (checked) in order for the Allow Invoice Processor to Process their own Invoices option to work.'

sequence.action: enable Allow Self Cost Object Approval
sequence.rationale: CORPUS-STATED: 'Allows the cost object approver to approve invoices regardless of whether they are the owner of the invoice or not.' (create-a-new-workflow-554e86aa.md), subject to the master gate quoted at order 11. DOCUMENTED NON-INTERACTION worth knowing here: 'The _prompt for approver_ setting has no affect within the cost object approval step.' (additional-approver-situations-fbb5034c.md) - do not expect the own-approver Settings control to influence this step.

sequence.action: on the Settings tab, decide whether cost object approvers see only their own line items
sequence.rationale: CORPUS-STATED: 'When selected, filters a Cost Object Approver's view to only those cost object line items and amount totals that apply to that approver; all others are removed from view.' (invoice-settings-cace748d.md, packed raw <table> row). INFERRED ordering: it is a Settings-tab control that applies globally, so it changes what EVERY cost object approver on every workflow sees - set it once, deliberately, after the workflow-level legs, and note enabling-and-disabling-an-invoice-workflow-setting-0e1e6d33.md's warning that 'The system applies the setting immediately.'

steps.name: Create a confirmation agreement and put it in force on submit and approve actions
steps.goal: Users and approvers must accept a legal disclaimer at submit and/or approve time. The corpus states the chain in one sentence - create, associate to the workflow, associate the workflow to the policy - and every link is required: an agreement with no workflow association never renders, and a workflow with no policy association is never used, so the agreement appears configured and no user ever sees it.

sequence.action: on the Confirmation Agreements tab click New and enter a unique internal name
sequence.rationale: CORPUS-STATED, and this is link 1 of the chain SAP states in one sentence: 'After creating the agreement, you associate the confirmation agreement with the workflow, and then associate the workflow with the policy.' (activating-the-confirmation-agreement-feature-bdfc1dce.md). The name is internal only - 'This name is used internally in the workflow; the user or approver cannot see this.' (create-a-confirmation-agreement-3e153f29.md) - so it is what the General-page lists at orders 6-7 match on, and must be distinctive enough to pick correctly there.

sequence.action: enter the title shown in bold above the message body
sequence.rationale: CORPUS-STATED: 'The text that is typed here appears in bold (no HTML tagging is required) and appears at the top of the message body area, directly below the title bar.' (create-a-confirmation-agreement-3e153f29.md). Unlike the name at order 1, THIS is what users see - conflating the two produces an agreement whose visible heading is an internal code.

sequence.action: enter the agreement text
sequence.rationale: CORPUS-STATED HARD LIMIT that constrains drafting before it constrains configuration: 'You may type up to 2000 characters.' (create-a-confirmation-agreement-3e153f29.md). The same row enumerates the HTML tags permitted inside this free-text field - those are markup allowed in the body, NOT selectable values for the control.

sequence.action: select the groups permitted to edit the agreement
sequence.rationale: CORPUS-STATED: 'Select the group or groups that can edit the agreement.' (create-a-confirmation-agreement-3e153f29.md). LABEL CASING TO EXPECT, verbatim from the corpus: this control is labelled 'Editable by Group(s)' with a lower-case 'by', unlike the General-page 'Editable By Group(s)' - a driver matching on exact label text must carry both forms.

sequence.action: save the Confirmation Agreement window
sequence.rationale: INFERRED from the create-then-associate ordering stated at activating-the-confirmation-agreement-feature-bdfc1dce.md ('After creating the agreement, you associate the confirmation agreement with the workflow'): the object must be committed before the workflow's General-page lists can offer it. Save is the shared commit control across the object-edit dialogs on this page.

sequence.action: open the workflow's General page and choose the agreement shown on submit
sequence.rationale: CORPUS-STATED, link 2 of the chain: 'In the Submit Confirmation Agreement list, choose the agreement to be displayed when submitting the invoice.' (activating-the-confirmation-agreement-feature-bdfc1dce.md). The list is populated from the Confirmation Agreements tab objects, so running this before orders 1-5 offers nothing to choose.

sequence.action: choose the agreement shown on approval actions
sequence.rationale: CORPUS-STATED, and a genuinely separate slot: 'In the Approval Confirmation Agreement list, choose the agreement to be displayed when approving the invoice.' (activating-the-confirmation-agreement-feature-bdfc1dce.md). Setting only the submit slot leaves approvers with no confirmation at all - the half-works case for this procedure.

sequence.action: click Done to commit the workflow
sequence.rationale: CORPUS-STATED: the association procedure ends 'Click Done.' (activating-the-confirmation-agreement-feature-bdfc1dce.md). INFERRED: the workflow must be committed before the policy at order 9 binds to the version carrying these two selections.

sequence.action: open the policy and select this workflow, then save
sequence.rationale: CORPUS-STATED, link 3 and the reason the whole chain can silently do nothing: 'then associate the workflow with the policy.' (activating-the-confirmation-agreement-feature-bdfc1dce.md). LABEL DRIFT IN THE SOURCE, recorded verbatim rather than smoothed: the same file's procedure says 'In the Expense Report Workflow list, choose the appropriate workflow.' while the built Policies page carries this control as Invoice Workflow - two labels in the corpus for the same association.

sequence.action: save the policy
sequence.rationale: CORPUS-STATED: 'Click Save.' (activating-the-confirmation-agreement-feature-bdfc1dce.md). ONE-WAY DOOR: after this save the workflow is assigned, and 'The system does not allow you to delete a workflow that is currently assigned to a policy.' (delete-a-workflow-or-workflow-steps-e9a84a07.md).

contradictions.topic: The Settings surface inside the Workflows page is named four different ways across four topics: 'Settings tab', 'Settings section of the Workflows tool', 'Workflow Settings page' and 'Settings page'.

readings.summary: Names it the Settings tab, inside a full click path - the only one of the four readings that carries a click path.
readings.sourceQuote: Settings tab and is shown in the following figure.

readings.summary: Names it the Settings section of the Workflows tool.
readings.sourceQuote: To set up the centralized workflow, you must clear a setting in the Settings section of the Workflows tool.

readings.summary: Names it the Workflow Settings page.
readings.sourceQuote: On the Workflow Settings page, select a setting option.

readings.summary: Names it the Settings page, in a cross-reference written from the General-page field roster.
readings.sourceQuote: field on the Settings page cleared (disabled)

contradictions.consequenceForWriter: Treat all four names as ONE surface and register all four as aliases of the Settings tab of the Workflows page. A driver must locate it by the visible string 'Settings' inside the Workflows page and must NOT go looking for a separate left-menu page called 'Workflow Settings' - a corpus-wide '(left menu)' census scores zero for that label. Never resolve any of the four to the already-built 'Invoice Settings' page: that is a different surface with a colliding title, and merging them would corrupt both.
contradictions.notes: Recon contradiction C1, carried forward with its readings re-grounded. Hypothesis (not a finding): four SAP guides written at different times each chose their own noun for the same tab, and the 'page' forms are writing drift rather than a second surface. The tables lens and the crosscut lens raised this independently; their readings are merged here, and where both cited the same file the longer, self-contained sentence was kept (the shorter crosscut quote 'you must clear a setting in the Settings section of the Workflows tool' is a substring of the kept one, so no evidence is lost).

contradictions.topic: The Authorized Approvers surface is named five different ways: 'Authorized Approvers tab' (plural), 'Authorized Approver tab' (singular), 'the Workflows, Authorized Approvers page', 'Authorized Approvers section of the Workflows tool' and 'Add Authorized Approvers page within Workflows'.

readings.summary: The singular tab name, inside a full Administration menu path.

readings.summary: Named as a page reached through the Workflows page, comma-separated rather than as a tab.
readings.sourceQuote: through the Workflows, Authorized Approvers page

readings.summary: Named as a section of the Workflows tool, twice in one sentence (and once as 'the Workflows tools', plural).
readings.sourceQuote: have set up in the Authorized Approvers section of the Workflows tool

readings.summary: Named as an 'Add Authorized Approvers page within Workflows' - a fifth form, with an added verb.
readings.sourceQuote: use the Add Authorized Approvers page within Workflows

readings.summary: A sub-tab structure is documented inside it, which is why 'tab' readings and 'page' readings can both feel right.
readings.sourceQuote: on the Configuration tab of the Authorized Approvers tab

contradictions.consequenceForWriter: Five labels, ONE surface: a tab of the Workflows page carrying two sub-tabs (Configuration and Authorized Approver List). Match on a case-insensitive prefix 'Authorized Approver' and never gate on the trailing 's'. Do not create a page node for any of the 'page' forms - all five readings resolve inside Workflows, including both singular ones, which give the parent path explicitly.
contradictions.notes: Recon contradiction C2, grounded here for the first time (no extraction lens raised it). Hypothesis: SAP topic prose uses 'page' loosely for any addressable screen area, and the singular/plural split is editorial. Counter-signal worth carrying: the two singular readings are the ones that spell out a full Administration path, so the singular form is not confined to casual prose.

contradictions.topic: The tab that lists workflow objects is 'Workflows tab' in fourteen topics and 'Workflow tab' in one - and the lone singular occurrence is inside a full Administration menu path.

readings.summary: Plural, as an executable click step in the canonical create-a-workflow procedure.
readings.sourceQuote: On the Workflows tab, select the desired workflow and click Copy.

readings.summary: Plural again, as the destination the access procedure asserts on.

readings.summary: Singular, and it is the only navigation the corpus gives for the Consolidate-items setting.
readings.sourceQuote: The setting appears in Administration > Invoice > Workflows > Workflow tab

contradictions.consequenceForWriter: Probe the plural 'Workflows' tab first - it carries fourteen topics including every click step - and accept the singular as an alias. Do not fail the Consolidate-items path because its only documented route names the tab in the singular.
contradictions.notes: Recon contradiction C3. Corpus weight is 14:1 by file count, which is why the plural is the primary probe; the count is not itself a quote and is recorded as context, not as a reading. Hypothesis: a one-off transcription slip. This is a DIFFERENT contradiction from the Workflow/Workflows PAGE drift recorded separately from administrator-experience-8b302852.md - that one is about the page, this one about the tab.

contradictions.topic: The email-template tab is 'Email Notification tab' (singular) in the create-a-workflow procedure and 'Email Notifications tab' (plural) everywhere else.

contradictions.consequenceForWriter: Probe the plural 'Email Notifications' first - it is the label used by the tab's own access topic and by every add/modify/remove procedure - and keep the singular as a fallback alias. Separately and more importantly: do NOT confuse this tab with the Email Reminders page, which is a different surface not yet built in this graph.
contradictions.notes: Recon contradiction C4. Hypothesis: the singular is a slip inside 554e86aa, which is the one topic that reaches the tab from elsewhere rather than documenting it directly. The singular/plural split recurs across this page for Confirmation Agreement(s), Authorized Approver(s), the Workflow(s) tab and the Workflow(s) page - it is a corpus-wide pattern, not a one-off.

contradictions.topic: The Confirmation Agreements tab is singular in one topic and plural in another - and the plural appears inside a file whose own title is singular.

readings.summary: The create procedure says the tab is the 'Confirmation Agreement' tab, singular.

readings.summary: The access topic instructs you to select the 'Confirmation Agreements' tab, plural - in a file whose own title uses the singular.

contradictions.consequenceForWriter: Register both 'Confirmation Agreement' and 'Confirmation Agreements' as tab aliases and match on the prefix. Never gate the step on the trailing 's'.
contradictions.notes: Recon contradiction C5, and independently raised by the tables lens. Hypothesis: SAP topic titles are habitually singular while the rendered UI is plural. Counter-evidence carried deliberately: access-the-confirmation-agreement-tab-666fa0ac.md is singular in its own filename and plural in its own click step, so the inconsistency exists INSIDE a single file and cannot be explained as a per-guide style difference.

contradictions.topic: The workflow wizard surfaces are called 'pages' in some topics, 'steps' in others and 'windows' in others - the same modal sequence, three different nouns.

readings.summary: The Steps-page topic calls the step editor a PAGE.
readings.sourceQuote: The Add Workflow Step page appears.

readings.summary: The authorized-approver-step topic calls the same editor, reached by the same New button, a WINDOW.
readings.sourceQuote: The Add Workflow Step window appears.

readings.summary: The create-a-workflow procedure calls the first wizard surface the General PAGE.
readings.sourceQuote: The General page appears.

readings.summary: The delegate-self-approval topic places a control on the General STEP of the same create/edit flow.
readings.sourceQuote: is available in the General step

readings.summary: The edit-and-reorder topic names the step editor in the PLURAL, as Modify Workflow Steps.
readings.sourceQuote: The Modify Workflow Steps window appears.

readings.summary: The level-assignment topic names the same editor in the SINGULAR, as Modify Workflow Step.
readings.sourceQuote: The Modify Workflow Step window appears.

contradictions.consequenceForWriter: Do not create separate nodes per noun: General page = General step; Add Workflow Step page = Add Workflow Step window; Modify Workflow Step = Modify Workflow Steps. Assert on the CONTROLS the surface offers, never on the word 'page', 'step' or 'window' in a heading, and never on the trailing 's'. These are wizard surfaces reached from inside Workflows, not pages in the graph's sense - the wizard returns you to the Workflows tab when done.
contradictions.notes: Recon contradiction C6. Kept as ONE node because the disagreement is a single one - what noun SAP uses for a wizard surface - expressed over three surfaces; splitting it into three would triple-count one editorial habit. Hypothesis: 'page' and 'window' reflect two UI generations of the same modal (a full page in one, a dialog in the other), which would make this a symptom of the unresolved UI-generation contradiction recorded separately. That is a hypothesis; no corpus sentence links them.

contradictions.topic: Two topics place General-page controls 'on the Workflows page' - the ancestor - while the General-page field table places the same controls on the General page.

readings.summary: The canonical procedure puts the fields on the General page, reached by copying a workflow from the Workflows tab, and its field table carries both Require Hardcopy Receipts and Steps Can Be Added By.

contradictions.consequenceForWriter: Do NOT create a second field node from the collapsed phrasing, and do not re-home these fields to the page root. To reach either control the driver must open a workflow from the Workflows tab first; 'on the Workflows page' is an abbreviation of that path, not an alternative location.
contradictions.notes: Recon contradiction C7. Hypothesis: feature-note topics name the top-level page because that is what a reader searches for, while the procedure names the wizard surface it actually opens. The same abbreviating habit is recorded independently at the navigation level, where five topics use the Invoice Processing Admin middle node and eight omit it - so abbreviation is this corpus's normal register, which is exactly why the collapsed form must not be read as a second location.

contradictions.topic: The Workflows navigation path is documented both with and without the 'Invoice Processing Admin' middle node, in the same corpus version.

readings.summary: With the middle node: the access topic routes through the Invoice Processing Admin menu.

readings.summary: With the middle node again, worded 'select' rather than 'click', in the Confirmation Agreement access topic.

Both forms end on the same page, so the driver should assert on the Workflows page appearing, not on the number of menu hops.
contradictions.notes: Recon contradiction C8. Hypothesis: SAP abbreviates the middle node in topics whose subject is not navigation. Note the two forms are not merely different words - one is a menu-then-item sequence and the other a single left-menu click, so a driver that hard-codes either shape will miss the other. This mirrors the middle-node treatment already applied to both Group 3 pages.

contradictions.topic: Which role may use the Workflows surface: the tool's own identity topic grants it to the Global and Group Invoice Configuration administrators, while the Reason Category and Codes tab REQUIRES the Invoice Configuration administrator (Restricted) role and then walks a write flow.

readings.summary: The Workflows tool identity topic grants view and use to the Global and Group Invoice Configuration administrators and never mentions a Restricted role.

If the automation ever hits a permission wall on Workflows, this tab is the likely cause.
contradictions.notes: Recon contradiction C9 - the most consequential one on this page - and independently raised by the crosscut lens. Hypothesis: the Restricted role was scoped to reason codes only and the two guides were never reconciled. A THIRD reading is reported to exist in a July 2025 release note making that same Restricted role read-only on Workflows with New/Copy/Remove disabled; release notes are not a citable sourceFile in this graph, so it is recorded here as unverified context, NOT as a reading. This is also why Reason Category and Codes was the closest page-hood call in the area: it is the one surface with a role gate different from the page's own.

contradictions.topic: Which UI generation the Workflows click paths describe: the guide's own revision history says the Workflows topics were rewritten to the new UI in place, while a tools-guides topic in the same corpus version says the administrator reaches Authorized Approvers in the classic interface.

readings.summary: The Workflows guide's revision history, dated September 2025, records that the images and text were updated to the NEW UI - implying the classic screens were replaced in place and no legacy twin survives.

readings.summary: A tools-guides topic in the same 2026_08 corpus says the administrator uses the Authorized Approvers link from workflows in the CLASSIC interface.

contradictions.consequenceForWriter: Set uiVariant 'undifferentiated' on every Workflows record and treat EVERY navPath on this page as unverified against a UI generation. Build the driver to try the documented path, detect failure, and re-read the live menu rather than asserting a route. This matters more than any single field: if the paths describe a superseded UI then every path on the page is wrong at once, and navigation is the one thing here that cannot be re-derived from the corpus. contradictions.notes: Inherited finding 6, raised independently by the tables lens and the crosscut lens with identical readings. contradictions.topic: The Cost-Object filter checkbox on the Settings tab is named for 'payment request items' in the settings table and for 'invoice items' in the guide's revision history.

readings.summary: The Settings-tab reference table - a raw <table> cell - names the control with 'payment request items'.

readings.summary: The Workflows guide's own revision history announces the same new Settings-tab option with 'invoice items'.
readings.sourceQuote: -   Filter invoice items to those that are applicable to Cost Object
